## Seeding the out-of-scope reading, and the order to read it in

*2026-09-25 20:42:31 · curation*

The seed entry of this afternoon left three questions open, and the owner
answered all three: **file all of it**, including the works that are not
papers; **seed from abstracts and skims**, then triage the result, because
the deeper readings still have to happen; and **when in doubt, the
anthology**. This entry records what the seeding did and the order the deeper
readings should take.

**29 works filed here, 5 to the anthology. 26 carry a `Skimmed` NOTE, 3 carry
none. Every LIT is `Deferred` ("Unreviewed"), with a status note saying it was
seeded and not read in full.**

## How it was done, and how far to trust it

Four agents each fetched one cluster's sources and wrote a dossier per work:
the bibliography, a paraphrased abstract, skim bullets each naming the
section or page it came from, what a deeper reading should check, a priority,
and what could and could not be reached. A script turned each dossier into a
LIT and, where the work was actually skimmed, a NOTE. The LIT's "Standing in
the record" keeps the priority, the checks and the access record, so the
triage below can be audited from the documents rather than from this entry.

**Depth was downgraded where the skim was not a skim.** The concussion review
(`LIT-029`) and Bourrat on individuality (`LIT-005`) were reached
only through a fetch tool that returns a model-written summary; the
publishers served a bot check. A summary of the text is not a skim of it, so
both are filed at abstract depth, with no NOTE. So is the wasp-venom
proteomics paper (`LIT-026`), where only the abstract was reachable.

**Identities corrected on the way.** The network-dimension paper the triage
called *Unveiling the Dimensionality of Networks of Networks* is filed under
the title it took in v2 and in *Phys. Rev. E* 114, L022301. The arXiv hash
`quant-ph/9601020` is Fuchs's 1995 PhD thesis. The two unnamed PDFs are
Bottke et al. on the Eulalia impact shower and Rungsa et al. 2016 in
*Toxicon*. The hearing transcript (`LIT-012`) matches the CourtListener
docket for D. Minn. 0:26-cv-00603 by case number and judge; the Drive copy
has not been checked against a docket entry, a transcript holds no ruling,
and whether a written order followed is unverified.

**The seven that are not papers.** The ISW report, JP 3-12, Drezner's essay
and Gelman's post carry `url:` sources. The three court documents carry
descriptive titles marked `[descriptive title]`, because a filing has a
caption, not a title.

## The five that went to the anthology

The seed named four boundary cases, and the owner's rule sent all four there.
A fifth joined them: *Rigor with Machine Learning from Field Theory to the
Poincaré Conjecture*, triaged under "other sciences", whose transferable
claim is methodological — let a learned model search and an exact procedure
verify what it finds. That is an `analysis-and-evaluation` claim, so it is in
doubt, so it is the anthology's. *Topos and Stacks* went under
`model-architecture` and `concept-geometry` rather than the
`analysis-and-evaluation` the seed guessed: it is about what an architecture
lets information and semantics do, not about how to measure anything.

That leaves `neuroscience` with no work under it as the primary topic, only
as the concussion review's second tag. The word stays; it was blurbed for a
cluster the reading feed keeps producing.

## Reading time is not the priority here, and why

The two largest totals in the whole feed are the Eulalia paper (11,500 s) and
the network-dimension letter (6,080 s), and their dossiers rank them low and
medium. That is not a contradiction: time measures the owner's attention, and
the priority below measures what a close reading would add to this record.

*Corrected the same evening.* This section first said the long totals meant
those works had "probably been read", and that a deeper-reading pass should
begin by asking the owner which NOTEs to mark `Read`. That misreads the
status. A NOTE records a reading *this record* made — `Read` is "the full
text, closely enough to state its assumptions and results exactly" — and it
is earned by doing that reading, not by the owner's attention in a browser
tab. The owner's reply: the status is an invitation to read the thing. So the
deeper readings below are this record's to perform, in this order, and a
`Skimmed` NOTE is replaced by a `Read` one when the reading is done.

## The order for deeper readings

**First — read in full.** Short, foundational, and each unlocks others.

1. **Spekkens, *Quasi-quantization*** (`LIT-007`, 1,615 s). The framing
   for the two later Spekkens-group papers. Read it before *Why interference
   phenomena…* (`LIT-019`) and the structure theorem (`LIT-003`),
   whose skims are enough once this is in hand. §II–III, the technical core,
   is what the skim missed.
2. **Abramsky & Brandenburger, the sheaf-theoretic structure of non-locality**
   (`LIT-016`). The core theorems are short. *Corrected by the reading
   ([NOTE-016](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-016.md)):* this entry first called it "this record's one bridge to the
   anthology", with *Topos and Stacks* building on it and sheaf neural
   networks descending from it. Neither holds. Belfiore & Bennequin cite it
   once, in a related-work list, and use nothing from it; the sheaf-network
   papers checked do not cite it. It is first on its own merits, as the
   founding and fully proved paper of its programme.
3. **The *U.S. v. Google* remedies opinion** (`LIT-006`, 1,040 s over
   four sessions). The skim did not reach the findings of fact on generative
   AI (pp. 17–46 — the entry first said 17–36): how a federal court understood LLMs, grounding and the GenAI
   market. That is the part worth reading.
4. **Mediano et al. and Varley & Hoel, side by side** (`LIT-025`,
   `LIT-027`, ~2,500 s combined). Two definitions of emergence from the
   same theme issue. A deeper reading is a comparison, and it should take in
   Rosas et al. 2020, the primary behind the first. Neither is the anthology's
   `capability-thresholds` sense of "emergence", and whoever reads them should
   write that down.

**Second — targeted sections, not the whole work.**

- Forman–Ricci curvature (`LIT-020`): the curvature formula and flow
  definitions, §2.3 and §4.
- Fuchs's thesis (`LIT-018`): chapters 2–3.
- Nested HDP (`LIT-002`): the SVI derivation in §4.
- The network-dimension letter (`LIT-028`): the Supplementary Material
  derivation, after asking whether it was already read.
- JP 3-12 (`LIT-015`): the definitions and the authorities chapter.
- The Rhode Island Hospital subpoena order (`LIT-024`): whether it was
  appealed, and how it interacts with the Texas enforcement order.
- Lindgren & Liukkonen (`LIT-001`): the linearization assumptions,
  against Nelson's stochastic mechanics.

**Third — the skim is enough unless an interest makes it otherwise.** The
remaining sixteen: Eulalia, wasp venom, vehicle routing, the emergence
theme-issue introduction, Betti Lagrangians, spectral sets, Ricci-flow
community detection, quantum thermodynamics, Pitman–Yor topic models, the two
Spekkens-group follow-ups named above, the concussion review, Bourrat, the ISW
report, the hearing transcript, Drezner and Gelman. Several of their
dossiers say the same thing: the value is in the primary sources the piece
cites, not in a second pass over the piece.

None of this promotes anything. A work leaves `Deferred` when somebody has
read it closely, and here nobody has yet.

## The first five close readings, and what the seed got wrong

*2026-09-25 21:30:54 · curation*

The first tier of the reading order in `2026/09/25/204231` is done. The owner's
correction set this pass in motion: `Read` is not a question for the owner
about their browser history. It is a status the record earns by reading the
work, and it is an invitation to do that. Five works were read in full, each by
one reader working from the full text and the seeded skim. Each skim NOTE
became a `Read` NOTE, at version 2, with a claims table and a section listing
what the full text contradicted. All five LITs left `Deferred` and are now
`Active`.

| LIT | NOTE | work | what the reading changed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `LIT-007` | `NOTE-013` | Spekkens, *Quasi-quantization* | The continuous-variable equivalence is with the *quadrature* subtheory, which sits strictly inside the Gaussian one, and not with "stabilizer/Gaussian". Table II's list of classically explainable phenomena is asserted, not derived. |
| `LIT-016` | `NOTE-016` | Abramsky & Brandenburger | The paper is **not a bridge** to the machine-learning work. The seed and this record's reading order both said it was. |
| `LIT-006` | `NOTE-004` | *U.S. v. Google* remedies opinion | The data remedy is far narrower than the skim said. The GenAI findings run to p. 46. The opinion holds the *opposite* of "search data is a moat for LLMs" (p. 156). |
| `LIT-025` | `NOTE-010` | Mediano et al., *Greater than the parts* | It is a restatement of Rosas et al. 2020 with no new theorem. The summary had inherited the review's overstatement that it "extends" that paper. |
| `LIT-027` | `NOTE-020` | Varley & Hoel, *Emergence as the conversion of information* | The headline conversion **reverses** for redundancy-leaning deterministic systems, and the Gaussian effect is 0.005–0.07. There are internal errors: a swapped figure caption, and a reference to a figure that does not exist. |

## The pattern

Every one of the five skims carried at least one claim the full text does not
support. Every one of those errors made the paper look **more connected, more
general or more conclusive** than it is. That is the drift the anthology's
`DP-010` warns about: the most citable sentence is often the least supported.
It also held on this record's own most-cited sentence. This record called
Abramsky & Brandenburger "this record's one bridge to the anthology", with
*Topos and Stacks* building on it and sheaf neural networks descending from it.
Belfiore & Bennequin cite it once, in a related-work list, and use nothing from
it. The two sheaf-network papers checked do not cite it at all. The claim was
corrected in place, in this record's reading order and in the anthology's
boundary entry, and each correction is marked as one.

The lesson for the seeding step is simple. A skim is honest about its depth,
but it is not honest about **connections**. A connection named from a skim is a
guess, and it should be written as one.

## What the reading turned up to file

**Rosas et al. 2020, *Reconciling emergences*** (*PLoS Comput. Biol.*), is the
primary source behind `LIT-025`. The review restates its theorem, and every
proof and assumption lives there. It is not held. It is the next filing in this
cluster, and `LIT-025` cannot be cited for the theorem until it is.

## Every work read but two, and what the readings did to the seed

*2026-09-25 22:10:08 · curation*

The reading order of `2026/09/25/204231` is done. **27 of the 29 works now
have a `Read` NOTE.** Each is written from the full text, with a claims table
and a section listing what the reading contradicted in the seed. The two left
over are the Toxicon venom proteomics paper (`LIT-026`) and the concussion
review (`LIT-029`). Neither is open access. Every route to a full text failed:
PMC and Europe PMC, the publishers, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and
ResearchGate. Both stay `Deferred` at abstract depth. Reading either needs a
PDF supplied by hand.

## Where the readings placed the works

| standing | count | works |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `Active` | 22 | the rest |
| `Proposed` | 3 | Bourrat (`LIT-005`), the Eulalia impact shower (`LIT-009`), Spectral Networks (`LIT-017`) |
| `Rejected` | 1 | Lindgren & Liukkonen (`LIT-001`) |
| `Deferred` | 2 | the two unobtainable works |

**Bourrat.** The measure it proposes is never computed on any system. Its
claim that the measure equals the observational one fails on a two-bit
counterexample: take S′ = S ⊕ E with uniform inputs. Then A = 1 bit, and the
interventional measure is 0.

**The Eulalia paper.** It is a plausibility model. Every lunar date scales
from one sample-dated crater. Its five fitted breakup ages span 785–965 Myr,
not the 800–900 its prose says.

**Spectral Networks.** It is unrefereed, and several theorem statements are
broader than their proofs.

**Lindgren & Liukkonen.** It puts the imaginary unit in twice by hand:
through √g instead of √(−g), and through a complex noise variance chosen to
force linearity.

## The pattern, held across all 27

Every skim carried at least one claim that the full text does not support.
Every one of those errors pointed in the same direction: toward the work being
more connected, more general or more conclusive than it is. The first five
readings (`2026/09/25/213054`) found this. Twenty-two more did not break it.
The corrections include:

- **Theorems stated more broadly than proved.** Ni et al.'s Theorem 4.1.
  Casals & Nho's Theorem 3.
- **Printed equations that do not do what the text says.**
  - Paisley et al.'s SVI update re-adds the prior at every step.
  - Weber et al.'s workflow silently uses the flow form the paper had just
    rejected.
  - Grimaldi et al.'s finite-size prefactors have the wrong power of N. A
    numerical check confirmed this.
- **Headline numbers the paper's own tables contradict.**
  - The Eulalia age range.
  - The waste-routing GA's "consistently" better routes.
  - The ~30% optimality gaps the skim left out.
- **Attributions that were syntheses.** The "Russian military definition" in
  the ISW report is Clark's composite, not a quotation.

Several readers also did their own arithmetic, and those checks are part of
the record:

- a comb-network simulation;
- a linear-programming check of a lemma;
- a Kesten–Stigum detectability calculation, which puts the stochastic
  block model's limit near 0.78, where Ni et al. read collapse as absence;
- ontic-state counts for the structure theorem, which match the GPT
  dimension exactly.

Where a reader went beyond the paper, its NOTE says so.

## Filing questions the readings raised

- **Rosas et al. 2020** is still the primary source behind `LIT-025`, and it is
  not held.
- **Levitsky & Way, *The Path to American Authoritarianism*** (Foreign Affairs,
  Feb 2025) is the primary source for most of Drezner's post (`LIT-022`), and
  it is not held.
- **JP 3-12** has a December 2022 revision. Secondary reports say it is
  restricted. If it is ever obtained, `LIT-015` becomes `Superseded` by it.
- **The Rhode Island order (`LIT-024`)** is on appeal in the First Circuit,
  with argument on 2026-10-07. The Texas enforcement order is on appeal in the
  Fifth. The record should be re-checked after either rules.

## First: read in full, in these pairs

1. **Bourrat's coarse-graining account of individuality ([LIT-049](../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md)),
   alongside his *Adding causality…* ([LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md), already read).** It is the same
   author's next move. *Corrected by the reading:* it is the same author's
   *earlier* move — received July 2022, published August 2023, and cited by
   [LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md) — so it cannot repair [LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md)'s defects; it holds the
   observational idea [LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md) later mis-equates with its interventional measure.
2. ***The Work Capacity of Channels with Memory* ([LIT-041](../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md)).** This is the
   anthology's one named decline. The skim found an
   information-thermodynamics theory: when actions affect what an agent later
   perceives, the agents that extract the most energy must trade prediction
   against forgetting. It carries no ML practice, which supports the decline.
   It went to Physical Review X in 2026, but the DOI Crossref lists has
   placeholder metadata, so it was left off until it can be confirmed.
3. **The linguistics triad:** Haspelmath on word segmentation ([LIT-063](../../record/literature.d/LIT-063.md)),
   Bruening ([LIT-071](../../record/literature.d/LIT-071.md)) and Krauska & Lau ([LIT-031](../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md)) against
   lexicalism. Haspelmath is filed under its 2011 first appearance, not the
   2017 reprint the survey found. It is the one work here with a plausible
   bearing on tokenization. That bearing is the seed reader's inference, not
   the paper's claim, so the work stays here unless a reading finds otherwise.

## The papers-feed swept for philosophy: 119 works seeded

*2026-09-26 05:58:20 · curation · record*

The owner asked for the papers-feed tracker's snapshot to be checked for more
philosophy to file, after Nagel ([LIT-096](../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md)). The owner also decided
that everything from the sweep stays here, and asked for anthology candidates
to be flagged with a tag. That tag is `anthology-candidate`, from
[ADR-005](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-005.md).

## The funnel

| stage | count |
| --- | ---: |
| papers in the snapshot (`gh-store-snapshot.json`) | 7,800 |
| scored as possibly philosophy | 217 |
| kept by hand, with duplicate captures merged | 132 |
| already held (the SEP entry on structural realism) | 1 |
| seed dossiers written, by six agents | 131 |
| dropped as not philosophy | 3 |
| merged as the same work under another capture | 9 |
| **filed, all `Deferred`** | **119** |

95 were skimmed from a full text and carry a `Skimmed` NOTE. 24 are seeded from
the abstract alone.

**How the score worked:**

- **Journal names:** *Synthese*, *Mind*, *Philosophy Compass*, *Biology &
  Philosophy*, *Minds and Machines* and the like.
- **Source URLs:** PhilPapers, PhilArchive, PhilSci-Archive, the SEP and JSTOR.
- **Keywords:** philosophy words in the title and the first 1,500 characters of
  the abstract.

*Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society* matches the journal filter
and is a science journal. Its hits were removed by hand.

**The score misses philosophy that carries no signal:** an arXiv paper in a
physics category, say, that never uses a philosophy word. A second pass over
the low scorers would find more. Nobody has made that pass.

**Three drops:**

- a political-science paper on propaganda technologies;
- a mathematics manuscript on Connes' rigidity conjecture, hiding behind an
  unresolved PhilPapers code;
- a JSTOR chapter on Hero of Alexandria's automata.

## Traps

- **PhilPapers, PhilArchive and Taylor & Francis are behind Cloudflare** from
  here. The tracker had captured about twenty of them as "Just a moment..." or
  as a bare hash, with no title.
  - The agents identified them from the PhilPapers code (an author-surname +
    title stem) and web search.
  - They read the texts through Wayback copies (`web.archive.org/web/2026id_/…`),
    author pages, PhilSci-Archive with a plain `curl` user agent, and
    `rd.springer.com`.
- **Duplicates only show once titles are resolved.** Seven of the nine merges
  were an unresolved PhilPapers capture of a work already in the batch under
  its journal URL: Wallace, Vetter, Floridi, Drayson, Šekrst, the
  distributional-semantics chapter, and the epistemic-injustice paper. So
  deduplicate *after* the seed, by DOI, arXiv id and title, never only before
  it. Reading time is pooled across the captures.
- **The dossiers cross-referenced each other by batch id** (`p078`). The filing
  script copied those into 150 files as-is. They were rewritten to the record's
  codes before commit.

## The vocabulary

Two words were added by [ADR-006](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-006.md):

- **`epistemology`**, used by fourteen works. One had no topic at all, and
  the rest had the nearest wrong one.
- **`logic`**, used by two.

A `philosophy-of-mind` word was considered and not added. The mental-causation
papers are honestly `metaphysics`.

**Two works are flagged `anthology-candidate`:**

- Terziyan et al., on ethics carried across generations of AI.

The borderline cases the dossiers kept here are:

- Mallory's *LLMs Are Stochastic Measuring Devices*.

## A pass over the mereology tag: four readings, eight retags

*2026-09-26 06:37:03 · curation · record*

The owner asked for a pass over the `mereology` tag. It held six works: two
read and four skimmed seeds from the morning's philosophy sweep. All four
seeds were read in full, and each is now `Active`:

| work | what the reading found |
| --- | --- |
| Varzi, SEP *Mereology* ([LIT-124](../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md)) | the formal reference: M ⊂ MM ⊂ EM ⊂ GEM, with the exact axioms. GEM is reached from M by exactly three pairings of a supplementation principle and a sum principle. |
| Carroll, *Reality as a Vector in Hilbert Space* ([LIT-123](../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md)) | a programme, not a result: parts are factorisations chosen afterwards, to suit the dynamics |
| Register, *The Depth of the Body* ([LIT-138](../../record/literature.d/LIT-138.md)) | a moral "body part" relation, bounded below by depth, applied to BCIs hosted in the cloud |
| Meincke, *One or two?* ([LIT-142](../../record/literature.d/LIT-142.md)) | process ontology keeps the foster as a part, and makes the count indeterminate |

## What the readings corrected

Each skim overstated its paper, in the same direction: a proposal was reported
as a result.

- **The SEP entry** was summarised as calling the partial-order core
  "uncontroversial". §2.1 says the opposite: all three core axioms have serious
  dissenters, and Antisymmetry "can hardly be regarded as constitutive".
- **Carroll** was credited with a uniqueness result for the quasi-classical
  factorisation. He does not claim one. The only uniqueness claim is for local
  factorisations, and it is borrowed from Cotler et al. Carroll's own criterion
  needs inputs beyond the spectrum, which he admits are "somewhat cheating".
  Fields were reported as "recovered". The essay only hopes to recover them.
- **Carroll's finiteness figure, e^(e^123),** is what the paper prints (p. 5).
  It does not follow from the paper's own premise, S = πr²/G, which gives a
  single exponential. Quote the order of magnitude, never the figure.
- **Register** was summarised as resting his ethics on the real-definition
  metaphysics and dissolving the ownership conflict. He says the principles do
  not depend on that ontology, and the conflict is narrowed, not dissolved.
- **Meincke** was summarised as offering a rival to the Parthood View. She keeps
  parthood and rejects only its pairing with substance ontology.

## Eight works that were about parts and wholes and did not say so

The tag's blurb reads "parts and wholes — composition, individuation of
systems and collectives". The test was whether someone browsing that topic
would expect the work. Eight held works pass, and now carry the tag after their
existing topics:

- **Composition of wholes:** [LIT-025](../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md) (ΦID causal emergence) and [LIT-027](../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md)
  (emergence as the conversion of information).
- **Constitution:** [LIT-097](../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md) (*The Extended Mind*).
- **Individuation:**
  - [LIT-157](../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md) (Bourrat, reproducees and reproducers)
  - [LIT-167](../../record/literature.d/LIT-167.md) (Baedke, *The Organism*)
  - [LIT-168](../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md) (SEP, *Biological Individuals*)
  - [LIT-188](../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md) (Griesemer & Shavit, scaffolding individuality)
- **A collective as a candidate subject:** [LIT-159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md) (Schwitzgebel, the United
  States as conscious).

Considered and not tagged: *Philosophy of Microbiology*, collective
intelligence and the ant/human puzzle study. They discuss collectives, but not
as a question about parts and wholes.

## The tag is wider than its reference

The SEP entry excludes two senses of "mereology":

- the systems-theory and ecological sense (its note 1);
- quantum part–whole formalisms (its note 18).

The tag's blurb names both on purpose: "individuation of systems and
collectives". So [LIT-124](../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md) is the background for the philosophical works on the
tag ([LIT-142](../../record/literature.d/LIT-142.md), [LIT-138](../../record/literature.d/LIT-138.md) and the individuality cluster). It is only loosely the
background for [LIT-123](../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md), [LIT-025](../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md) and [LIT-027](../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md), which use "part" for a tensor
factor or a coarse-grained variable. A reader should not expect the SEP's
axioms to hold of those.

## Still open on the tag

- **The two Bourrat papers** ([LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md), [LIT-049](../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md)) remain `Proposed`. Each would
  be settled by a worked model: an explicit computation of its individuality
  measure on a model of an evolutionary transition. Another reading cannot
  supply that.
- **Six of the newly tagged works are still `Deferred`:** the four
  individuality works, *The Extended Mind* and Schwitzgebel. They are the
  natural next readings for this tag.

## The mereology tag's newly tagged works, read

*2026-09-26 06:50:21 · curation · record*

The earlier pass over the tag (the previous entry) added eight works whose
subject is parts and wholes. Two of them, [LIT-025](../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md) and [LIT-027](../../record/literature.d/LIT-027.md), had already been
read. The other six are now read in full:

| work | status | what the reading found |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SEP, *Biological Individuals* ([LIT-168](../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md)) | Active | Wilson & Barker's own nine-region framework: organism / some parts / some groups, crossed with living agent / Darwinian individual. It never defines "part" and gives no rule for which parts or groups count. |
| Bourrat, *Reproducees, reproducers, and Darwinian individuals* ([LIT-157](../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md)) | Active | nested statuses, with material overlap necessary for reproducers but not reproducees. Its measures are recipes, never computed. |
| Baedke, *The Organism* ([LIT-167](../../record/literature.d/LIT-167.md)) | Active | the clearest statement of persisters vs overcomers. Separation from the environment is [LIT-110](../../record/literature.d/LIT-110.md)'s model, re-presented. |
| Griesemer & Shavit, *Scaffolding individuality* ([LIT-188](../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md)) | Proposed | a sketch. Its non-circularity is one sentence in the abstract, and its third stage presupposes the group. |
| Schwitzgebel, *If materialism is true…* ([LIT-159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md)) | Active | a whole of conscious parts can be conscious; it rejects anti-nesting, including IIT's exclusion postulate |
| Clark & Chalmers, *The Extended Mind* ([LIT-097](../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md)) | Active | the step from coupling to parthood rests on assumed functionalism and a proposal about the word "belief". "Part" is never given a mereological sense. |

## What the readings corrected

The skims overstated in the same direction as the first pass found: a proposal
was reported as a result, or a sufficient condition as a list of paradigm
features.

- **Clark & Chalmers' conditions** on a coupled resource were summarised as
  sufficient ("provided…"). The paper says it gives no "categorical answers".
- **Schwitzgebel's §6** does not test the Dretske, Dennett, Humphrey and Tononi
  theories. It rebuts four objections, Chalmers's the most seriously.
- **Bourrat's dossier** had reproductive causal control evolving through
  scaffolding. The paper (p. 21) says scaffolded collectives get control for
  free, and that what must evolve is autonomy.
- **The SEP entry's framework** was credited to Pepper & Herron, who only pose
  the question.

## Where the works disagree

- **Genes.** Bourrat ([LIT-157](../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md)) makes genes, like hearts, mere reproducees. The
  SEP entry ([LIT-168](../../record/literature.d/LIT-168.md)) places genes as Darwinian individuals. The record holds
  both. Neither is retired.
- **Bourrat against his own earlier papers** ([LIT-005](../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md), [LIT-049](../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md)):
  - *Inherited:* nothing is computed; the environment is handled by
    conditioning; and the control measure is biased toward fine grains.
  - *Fixed:* autonomy (associational) and control (interventional) are kept
    apart.
  - *Scale rule:* "smallest object at maximal MI" runs opposite to [LIT-049](../../record/literature.d/LIT-049.md)'s
    coarsest grain.

## A defect found and fixed along the way

The script that writes a Read NOTE rewrites the LIT's summary. It kept a
citation head only when the head ended in ")." or ">.". For "Clark et al.
(1998), DOI-10.1093/analys/58.1.7." it fell back to splitting at the first
". ", and kept only "Clark et al.". That dropped the year and the identifier.

## A pass over the metaphysics tag: thirty-two readings, two new topics

*2026-09-26 19:01:09 · curation · record*

The owner asked for a pass over `metaphysics`, after `mereology` and
`agency`. The tag held 45 works: 16 read, 27 skimmed seeds and 2 seeded
from the abstract. The 29 unread went to seven close readers, grouped by
cluster. The coverage audit added four works to the tag, and the three of
them that were unread went to an eighth reader.

## Outcome

- **Read in full: 30.**
  - **Active: 27.**
  - **Proposed: 1.** Allori, *Wave-functionalism* ([LIT-200](../../record/literature.d/LIT-200.md)). Its claim to
    bypass PBR is asserted in one footnote. It is also inconsistent about
    whether ψ is nomological.
  - **Rejected: 2.**
    - Karpenko ([LIT-215](../../record/literature.d/LIT-215.md)). It misreads Floridi three ways. It says an
      AdS/CFT boundary theory is two-dimensional, and that a quantum field
      operator obeys the Schrödinger equation. Its abstract's "it is proven"
      has no argument behind it.
    - The pregeometry paper by Arsiwalla, Elshatlawy & Rickles ([LIT-102](../../record/literature.d/LIT-102.md)).
      Nothing in it is constructed; the "link" it draws is a summary of
      other programmes. The same group's observers paper ([LIT-133](../../record/literature.d/LIT-133.md)) was
      Rejected in the agency pass.
- **Not obtainable: 2.** Pernu 2015 ([LIT-144](../../record/literature.d/LIT-144.md)) and Carson's Element
  ([LIT-104](../../record/literature.d/LIT-104.md)). Both stay `Deferred`, with the attempts in their status notes.
  Pernu's open 2013 dissertation (HELDA) covers the same argument at an
  earlier stage.

**The skims again overstated in the same direction:** a programme or proposal
was reported as a result. The most consequential cases:

- **Chakravartty ([LIT-196](../../record/literature.d/LIT-196.md))** says outright that nothing in the chapter tells
  against *eliminative* OSR. The skim had it collapsing the view into
  eliminativism.
- **Gao's 194-page monograph ([LIT-121](../../record/literature.d/LIT-121.md))** gives three routes to ψ-reality. All
  three rest on one premise that his own fn. 10 undercuts.
- **Holik et al. ([LIT-107](../../record/literature.d/LIT-107.md))** do not derive the Indistinguishability Principle.
  They move it into a postulate, and two printed proofs contain errors.
- **Barrett et al. on IIT ([LIT-185](../../record/literature.d/LIT-185.md))** concede that IIT 4.0 does say "high Φ =
  more consciousness". Their multi-dimensional measure is a proposed
  revision of the theory.
- **The SEP *Personal Identity and Ethics* ([LIT-130](../../record/literature.d/LIT-130.md))** shows the metaphysics
  constraining the ethics but rarely settling it. The current entry, Dufner
  2025, also replaced Shoemaker's at the same URL.
- **De Haro & Butterfield ([LIT-199](../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md))** say AdS/CFT is an exception only to
  duality being compatible *solely* with epistemic emergence. It is not an
  exception to "dualities are not indicative of emergence".
- **Hazelwood ([LIT-156](../../record/literature.d/LIT-156.md))** targets Laland and colleagues, not [LIT-110](../../record/literature.d/LIT-110.md). [LIT-110](../../record/literature.d/LIT-110.md)'s
  own standing note, which said otherwise, is corrected.
- **Rizi ([LIT-150](../../record/literature.d/LIT-150.md)) and McKenzie ([LIT-141](../../record/literature.d/LIT-141.md))** both lean on LLM "emergent
  abilities".
  - Rizi does so in one unhedged sentence. Its example is arithmetic, the
    case Schaeffer et al. ([ANTH-LIT-471](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-471.md)) show to be a metric artefact.
  - McKenzie examines the question (§21.2), and still calls Wei et al.
    ([ANTH-LIT-470](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-470.md)) "concrete and rigorous".

    different question, and its GPT tests report no settings.

## What the pass established

- **Birch and Seth answer each other.** Birch's v4 names Seth, and its §12
  overlaps his BBS commentary on Seth. They disagree on four things:
  - whether the illusion that an AI is conscious can be blocked at the level
    of belief (Birch: yes; Seth: perhaps not, like Müller-Lyer);
  - how likely consciousness is in current LLMs;
  - whether a link between consciousness and life is testable;
  - what a global workspace found in an LLM would show.

  They agree on Nagel's definition ([LIT-096](../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md)) and on treating LLMs as
  role-players.
- **Schwitzgebel's arguments are layered.** *The Weirdness of the World*
  collects the earlier arguments. [LIT-159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md) is its chapter 2 in manuscript and
  chapter 3 in print, revised: the IIT footnote is much expanded and now
  engages the expander-graph case that [LIT-185](../../record/literature.d/LIT-185.md) defends against. *AI and
  Consciousness* ([LIT-191](../../record/literature.d/LIT-191.md)) continues its chapters 10 and 11. [LIT-159](../../record/literature.d/LIT-159.md) now says so.
- **Kleiner & Ludwig's published version drops a result.** The finding that
  metric spaces are not structures of experience is only in arXiv v1 §4.
  Cite the preprint for it.
- **Veit now rejects plant consciousness.** That conflicts with the paper he
  co-wrote, [LIT-193](../../record/literature.d/LIT-193.md).

<a id="20260926202345"></a>

## Ladyman and Ross on the record: ontic structural realism and rainforest realism

*2026-09-26 20:23:45 · curation · record*

The owner asked for James Ladyman and Don Ross's accounts of **ontic
structural realism (OSR)** and **rainforest realism** to be on the record,
ideally from their book *Every Thing Must Go: Metaphysics Naturalized* (OUP
2007, with Spurrett and Collier).

## What could not be obtained

Only legitimate sources were used: publishers, repositories, the authors' own
pages and the Wayback Machine. Shadow libraries were ruled out.

- ***Every Thing Must Go*.** Not open access, and OUP returned 403. No free
  sample was found. An archive.org upload labelled "Public Domain" is an
  unauthorised copy and was not used.
- **Ladyman 1998, "What is structural realism?"** (SHPS), the founding OSR
  paper. Paywalled, with no repository copy.
- **Ross 2000, "Rainforest Realism: a Dennettian theory of existence"** (in
  *Dennett's Philosophy*, MIT). Closed access.
- **Berenstain & Ladyman 2012, "Ontic Structural Realism and Modality".**
  On PhilArchive, which blocked this session, as did the Wayback Machine.

## What was read instead

Four freely available works, each read in full and `Active`:

| work | what it contributes |
| --- | --- |
| Ladyman 2001, *Science, Metaphysics and Structural Realism* ([LIT-217](../../record/literature.d/LIT-217.md)) | the earliest free statement of OSR by its founder |
| Ladyman, *Patterns All the Way Up* (2024 preprint, MIT 2026) ([LIT-219](../../record/literature.d/LIT-219.md)) | the core of rainforest realism, and his current second thoughts |
| Ross 2008, *Ontic Structural Realism and Economics* ([LIT-218](../../record/literature.d/LIT-218.md)) | OSR carried beyond physics |
| Dennett 1991, *Real Patterns* ([LIT-220](../../record/literature.d/LIT-220.md)) | the criterion that rainforest realism generalises. Read because Ross 2000 was unreachable. |

**What each supplies:**

- **Ladyman 2001:**
  - the quantum non-individuality argument, framed as an underdetermination
    between individuals and non-individuals, not a proof;
  - entanglement against Humean supervenience;
  - theories describing "the modal structure of the phenomena";
  - a non-eliminative line: "the phenomena have structure but they are not
    structure".
- ***Patterns All the Way Up*:**
  - "to be is to be a real pattern";
  - scale-relative, effective ontology;
  - no single hierarchy of levels;
  - agnosticism, not denial, about a fundamental level (fn. 9);
  - the Principle of Naturalistic Closure quoted from the book (p. 37), then
    called "problematic" by Ladyman himself.
- **Ross 2008:** individuals are "book-keeping devices", not denied. That is a
  deflationary third position, which Chakravartty's dilemma ([LIT-196](../../record/literature.d/LIT-196.md)) does not
  address.
- **Dennett 1991:** a pattern is real iff some description beats the bit map,
  "whether or not anyone can concoct it". Rival real patterns can coexist.

## How far the two ideas are covered

- **OSR:** covered by the new works together with [LIT-045](../../record/literature.d/LIT-045.md) (the SEP entry, by
  Ladyman) and [LIT-196](../../record/literature.d/LIT-196.md). The explicit eliminative/non-eliminative choice still
  rests on those two held notes: no new text by the authors stakes it out.
- **Rainforest realism:** covered for real patterns, scale relativity, the
  rejection of a fundamental level of individuals, and the PNC.

**Gaps:**

- The **Primacy of Physics Constraint** is stated in none of the four.
- The **book's own real-patterns definition** (Ross 2000 and *Every Thing
  Must Go*), which adds projectibility to Dennett's compression, is referred
  to but not quoted.

The book, Ross 2000, or Berenstain & Ladyman would close both. Berenstain &
Ladyman is the one to try first, from a session that can reach PhilArchive.

## Corrections the readings raise

These are recorded here, not written into the older notes, because each is
about what the *new* sources say.

- **[NOTE-038](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-038.md) and [NOTE-129](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-129.md)** credit the projectibility and perspective clauses
  to "real patterns" in general. Dennett's own criterion is plain lossless
  compression.
- **[NOTE-129](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-129.md) has Ladyman and Ross "deny" a fundamental level.** *Patterns All
  the Way Up* fn. 9 says they are agnostic about one. That may be a later
  retreat, or a misreading; the book would settle which.
- **The record's two accounts of real patterns disagree** on whether the
  fundamental level is itself a pattern: Wallace ([LIT-151](../../record/literature.d/LIT-151.md)) against Ladyman &
  Lorenzetti ([LIT-184](../../record/literature.d/LIT-184.md)). *Patterns All the Way Up* states the disagreement.

<a id="20260926205202"></a>

## The Yoneda lemma, and whether it supports ontic structural realism

*2026-09-26 20:52:02 · curation · record*

The owner asked for an account of the Yoneda lemma, connected if possible to
ontic structural realism (OSR). Three works were filed and read in full, all
`Active`:

| work | why |
| --- | --- |
| nLab, *Yoneda lemma* ([LIT-221](../../record/literature.d/LIT-221.md)) | the lemma stated and proved, with the embedding as fully faithful and the corollary y(c) ≅ y(d) ⇔ c ≅ d, in a self-contained unit that can be read whole |
| Bain 2013, *Category-theoretic structure and radical ontic structural realism* ([LIT-223](../../record/literature.d/LIT-223.md)) | the main category-theoretic argument for *radical* (eliminative) OSR |
| Lam & Wüthrich 2015, *No categorial support for radical ontic structural realism* ([LIT-222](../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md)) | the reply. It `corrects` Bain in the record's relation graph. |

## The finding: no source in the core literature names Yoneda

Neither Bain nor Lam & Wüthrich mentions the Yoneda lemma, representable
functors or universal properties. Lal & Teh (arXiv:1404.3049), searched in
full text, does not either. Eva 2016 (EJPS) could not be obtained from a
legitimate free source.

- **Bain stops one step short.** He quotes Awodey on objects "determined …
  by their position in a structure", and defines products by probing them
  from outside, but never takes the step to the lemma.
- **Lam & Wüthrich use two of its consequences without the name.**
  Generalised elements X → A exist in every category, and morphisms "only
  distinguish isomorphism classes of structures".

Two works that do name the lemma were found and **not filed**:

- **Adlam 2025 (arXiv:2507.20313).** One sentence: Yoneda "implies that
  objects may emerge from the 'morphisms'". The source it cites, Yokura 2017,
  was read in full and says nothing of the kind.
- **Hendren, Grasso, Ellia & Tononi 2026 (arXiv:2608.24928).** A box calls
  Yoneda OSR's "mathematical centerpiece". That is an assertion, and the paper
  is about qualia, not physics.

## What the lemma does and does not support

The lemma says an object is determined **up to isomorphism** by its hom-functor,
its relations to every other object. That supports **objects as positions in a
structure**: the non-eliminative OSR of Ladyman 2001 ([LIT-217](../../record/literature.d/LIT-217.md)), and Lam &
Wüthrich's "balanced" OSR. It does **not** support radical OSR, for three
reasons:

1. **The determination presupposes the category's objects.** The hom-functor
   is indexed by them, and the conclusion is an isomorphism between two of
   them.
2. **It needs the composition structure, not merely which hom-sets exist.**
   The nLab page's own counterexample has two non-isomorphic objects whose
   hom-sets are in bijection at every object.
3. **It fixes objects only up to isomorphism.** That is the categorical twin
   of the limit on weak discernibility in Leitgeb & Ladyman ([LIT-154](../../record/literature.d/LIT-154.md)).

So Bain's inference to eliminating objects is overstated. His reliance on
elements as arrows out of a terminal object also fails once generalised
elements are admitted.

## Errors the readings found in the works

- **nLab:** its finite counterexample breaks the identity law as written, and
  its HoTT proof has small errors. It gives only the presheaf form.
  Nat(Hom(A,−),F) ≅ F(A) follows by passing to C^op.
- **Bain:** treats sections of a sheaf of Einstein algebras as maximal ideals,
  and mis-defines a maximal ideal.
- **Both papers:** say Hilb has no products. Direct sums are products.
- **Lam & Wüthrich:** mis-define a topos, and say non-commutative algebras
  have no maximal ideals.

The corrections, as in the epistemology pass, mostly took claims away from the
seeds:

- **Veit.** The skim had him "conceding" that Kukla can hold the institution
  of medicine fixed. That is the second horn of his own dilemma: holding
  medicine fixed makes the account normativist "in name only".
- **Schmauder et al.** The seed said AI systems "can learn nudges that exploit
  biases nobody has documented". Both case studies exploit documented biases.
  The undocumented case is a conjecture.
- **Hooker.** The seed had the view survive by "acceptance by less than
  everyone and a prevent-disaster rule". That misassigns the replies. Ranking
  rules by the expected good of teaching and accepting them answers the
  collapse objection. The prevent-disaster rule answers only rule-worship. The
  90% threshold is there for punishment rules.

## Representation learning, description length and Riesz: an owner's reading list filed

*2026-09-26 23:15:41 · curation · record*

The owner asked for a list of 24 works to be filed, grouped under their own

The Kolmogorov-complexity and MDL theory, the compression bounds, the Riesz

## Corrections the seeds made to the list

The list's venues and identifiers were checked against the works:

- **Knowledge sheaves** appeared at AISTATS 2023, not 2021. 2021 is the year of
  arXiv v1.
- **Assran et al.** is an ICLR 2023 poster, and **Tan et al.** appeared at
  ICLR 2024. The list gave "arXiv" for both.
- **Sun et al.** was in the ICML 2023 proceedings before its arXiv posting.
- **Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski** first appeared at NeurIPS 2023.
- **Simon et al.** is arXiv 2303.15438.

  that it contains errors, and has no journal version.

## One relation

Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski argue that Vera et al.'s bound on I(X;U) is
vacuous in realistic settings. It is recorded as `corrects`. The claim comes
from a skim, and a reading should confirm it.

## "Do we even need Riesz?"

The owner's note under the Riesz heading asked this. The dossier agent's
answer, from reading the four pages: **yes, as a lemma, not as a reading.**

- Riesz is what makes kernels exist. Evaluation at a point is a continuous
  functional, and Riesz turns it into the kernel vector k_x.
- It is why a linear probe or "concept direction" can be treated as a vector.
- It is why adjoints, and so the spectral arguments in the self-supervised
  learning papers, make sense.
- Adler's REU paper ends on Radon–Nikodym, the density result that KL
  divergence and mutual information, and so the bottlenecks, rest on.
- Bra–ket is notation.
- GNS is a suggestive analogy: a state determines its representation up to
  unitary equivalence. That echoes the Platonic hypothesis's kernel
  comparisons, but no representation-learning paper found uses it.

None of the four pages makes these connections itself. They are the dossier's
own and are marked as such.

<a id="20260926234228"></a>

## Riesz, Radon–Nikodym and GNS in representation learning: the connections pursued

*2026-09-26 23:42:28 · curation · record*

The owner filed the Riesz representation theorem, bra–ket notation and the GNS
construction next to a reading list on representation learning, and asked "do
we even need Riesz?". A dossier agent answered with four connections:

- Riesz makes kernels exist;
- a linear probe is a functional, and so a vector;
- Radon–Nikodym underwrites KL, mutual information and the bottlenecks;
- GNS says a state determines its representation up to unitary equivalence,
  echoing the Platonic hypothesis.

The source pages made none of these connections themselves. The owner asked
for them to be expanded and pursued. Three research agents took one strand
each and read the relevant theorems in the papers' own texts:

- Riesz and reproducing kernels;
- Radon–Nikodym and density ratios;
- GNS and unitary equivalence.

## The one object the strands meet in

The three strands converge on a single object: the positive-pair density ratio
K⁺(a,b) = p⁺(a,b) / (p(a)p(b)). It is four things at once.

1. **A Radon–Nikodym derivative.** It is dP⁺/d(P⊗P), and InfoNCE, the
   logistic loss and the spectral contrastive loss all have it as their
   population optimum. InfoNCE and skip-gram reach it in the log domain, as PMI
   ([THEORY-001](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md)).
2. **A Mercer kernel.** Its kernel principal components are the eigenfunctions
   of the positive-pair Markov chain. Their span is the minimax-optimal linear
   basis for view-invariant targets ([THEORY-007](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-007.md)).
3. **The kernel of the conditional-expectation operator on L²(p).** The
   record's own derivation: (Tf)(a) = E[f(A′) | A = a] = ∫ K⁺(a,b) f(b) p(b)
   db. T is Hilbert–Schmidt exactly when 1 + χ²(P⁺‖P⊗P) < ∞. L²(p) is the
   space the commutative GNS construction builds from the state f ↦ E_p f
   ([THEORY-005](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md), Proposed: no source states this whole).
4. **The exponential of the PMI kernel.** Huh et al.'s Platonic hypothesis
   proves convergence to the PMI kernel under its assumptions ([ANTH-LIT-458](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-458.md),
   §4.2).

The owner's reading list therefore has one topic under four headings. The
spectral self-supervised learning papers, the density-ratio view of
contrastive learning, and the Platonic hypothesis all describe the same
operator.

## Answers, connection by connection

**Riesz makes kernels exist: true, and stated.** Muandet et al. ([LIT-260](../../record/literature.d/LIT-260.md))
state Riesz (Thm 2.4) and derive the reproducing property from it
(Prop. 2.1).

- **The kernel mean embedding is a Riesz representer.** It is the representer
  of taking an expectation (Lemma 3.1). This is the one place in the family
  where Riesz is invoked by name.
- **Self-supervised learning can be read as separating mean embeddings.** Li
  et al.'s SSL-HSIC ([LIT-248](../../record/literature.d/LIT-248.md)) turns this into an objective: it maximizes the
  average squared MMD between each image's view distribution ([THEORY-003](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-003.md)).

Two parts of the original connection did not survive:

- **The representer theorem does not use Riesz.** Schölkopf, Herbrich &
  Smola's proof ([LIT-261](../../record/literature.d/LIT-261.md)) uses the reproducing property and orthogonal
  projection instead.
- **No spectral SSL paper invokes Riesz.** Their self-adjointness comes from
  the symmetry of the positive-pair distribution ([THEORY-009](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md)).

**So, do we need Riesz?** Yes, for defining a reproducing-kernel space
abstractly, for kernel mean embeddings, and for the adjoint of a general
bounded operator. No, for the finite-space spectral theorems the
self-supervised learning papers actually prove.

**Asymmetric methods are where Riesz would earn its keep.** Predictor and
stop-gradient methods (BYOL, SimSiam) and cross-modal pairs (CLIP) are not
covered by the symmetric theory. There the natural object is the singular
value decomposition of a non-self-adjoint operator, which needs the adjoint in
earnest. No such account was found. That is the open question worth pursuing
next.

**A probe is a functional: true, finite-dimensional, and already held.** Park,
Choe & Veitch ([ANTH-LIT-606](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-606.md)) use a "Riesz isomorphism" to map a concept's
probe direction to its steering vector. Their substance is that training does
not fix the inner product.

Harvey, Lipshutz & Williams ([LIT-257](../../record/literature.d/LIT-257.md)) prove the representation-side fact.
What a regularized linear readout decodes depends only on the representation's
normalized kernel. CKA, CCA and GULP are averages of readout agreement ([THEORY-008](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)).

No paper treats probes on an infinite-dimensional feature space as bounded
functionals.

**Radon–Nikodym underwrites mutual information: true.** Belghazi et al.
([LIT-256](../../record/literature.d/LIT-256.md)) write mutual information as the expected log Radon–Nikodym
derivative. The Donsker–Varadhan bound is tight exactly there.

Poole et al. ([LIT-246](../../record/literature.d/LIT-246.md)) prove that InfoNCE lower-bounds mutual information for
every critic and never exceeds log K ([THEORY-006](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-006.md)). Tschannen et al.
([LIT-247](../../record/literature.d/LIT-247.md)) show that tightening the bound does not explain why the
representations are good.

Two caveats from this strand:

- The conditional entropy bottleneck ([LIT-226](../../record/literature.d/LIT-226.md)) works with entropies, not the
  Radon–Nikodym form.
- Vera et al. ([LIT-240](../../record/literature.d/LIT-240.md)) could not be read, so whether it states the
  absolute-continuity condition is unverified.

**GNS: true as a parallel, stated by one source, and used by no
representation-learning paper.** Jorgensen & Tian ([LIT-259](../../record/literature.d/LIT-259.md)) name the
kernel-to-Hilbert-space construction "the GNS construction" (Remark 1.34).
They prove a kernel's minimal realizations are unique up to a unitary
(Cor. 1.35).

On the representation side:

- Harvey, Larsen & Williams ([LIT-250](../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md)) prove that Procrustes distance equals
  the Bures distance between kernels ([THEORY-004](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)). So the kernel is the
  invariant, and a representation is one realization of it.
- Nielsen et al. ([LIT-253](../../record/literature.d/LIT-253.md)) show that a softmax model's distribution fixes its
  embeddings only up to an invertible linear map. Closeness in KL does not
  bound representational dissimilarity.
- The Platonic hypothesis's convergence, read carefully, is convergence of
  kernels, up to the symmetry group of whatever is observed ([THEORY-002](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md),
  Proposed).
- Huh et al. measure with mutual nearest neighbours, which is much weaker than
  kernel equality.

The strand's own caveat stands: GNS of E_p gives L²(p), which contains no
learned representation. What connects them is the training objective, through
the density ratio.

## Status of what was filed

- **Works: sixteen, all `Deferred` with `Skimmed` notes.** Two works were
  found by two strands (HaoChen et al., Johnson et al.). Each is filed once,
  with both skims in its note.
- **THEORY documents: nine, all `Proposed`.** Six are theorems proved in
  their sources that this record has only skimmed; each promotes on a close
  reading. Three are inferences across papers, and each names the kind of
  result that would settle it.
- **Relations.** The operator claim and the self-adjointness claim extend the
  eigenbasis claim, which extends the shared-optimum claim. The readout and
  Platonic claims extend the kernel-invariance claim.

## Open questions the strands left

- Are Simon et al.'s NTK-based kernel ([LIT-242](../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md)) and K⁺ the same operator in
  any limit? Simon et al. say their representations differ from the
  optimum-based accounts.
- Rank-d truncation of PMI versus of exp(PMI): do InfoNCE-style and
  spectral-style representations differ in the top-d subspace? No paper
  compares them.
- Is χ²(P⁺‖P⊗P) < ∞ stated anywhere as the condition for the spectral account
  on continuous inputs?
- Do models with high mutual-nearest-neighbour alignment also have high Bures
  alignment of their centred kernels?
- Worth filing next: NeuralEF (arXiv 2205.00165, read but not filed), its
  follow-up (arXiv 2210.12637), Aronszajn (1950), and Wang & Isola's
  alignment/uniformity paper. Whether its uniformity term is a squared
  mean-embedding norm is unchecked.

<a id="20260927021945"></a>

## Contextuality: the threads brought together

*2026-09-27 02:19:45 · curation · record*

The owner asked whether the record had an account of contextuality. It had the
works: five were read in full. What it lacked was the account: no tag to find
them by, and nothing connecting the two formal threads they form.

The owner asked for the tag, and for the threads to be brought together with
theory entries. [ADR-012](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-012.md) adds the tag. A research agent read the five works'
notes and, where needed, the texts. It drafted the claims below and seeded the
four bridging works the record lacked:

- Spekkens (2005), the bridge between the two notions ([LIT-266](../../record/literature.d/LIT-266.md));
- Abramsky, Barbosa & Mansfield's contextual fraction ([LIT-265](../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md));
- Budroni et al.'s 2022 review ([LIT-263](../../record/literature.d/LIT-263.md));
- Dzhafarov, Zhang & Kujala on behavioural and social data ([LIT-264](../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md)).

## The account in seven claims

| claim | status |
| --- | --- |
| [THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md): Kochen–Specker contextuality is the failure of context distributions to glue into one global distribution. Signed ones always exist, so negativity is no marker. | Active ([LIT-016](../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md), read) |
| [THEORY-016](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-016.md): generalized noncontextuality is equivalent to a positive quasiprobability representation, which is a rigid, exact frame. | Active ([LIT-003](../../record/literature.d/LIT-003.md), read) |
| [THEORY-015](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-015.md): Kochen–Specker noncontextuality is measurement noncontextuality plus outcome determinism, and preparation noncontextuality forces the determinism. Every Kochen–Specker proof therefore refutes the universal notion. | Proposed (Spekkens 2005, skimmed) |
| [THEORY-011](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-011.md): the generalized notion is strictly broader: a qubit is already preparation-contextual. | Proposed (skimmed) |
| [THEORY-014](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-014.md): in both formalisms, classicality is positivity of a representation that always exists over the reals. | Proposed (the record's inference joining two read theorems) |
| [THEORY-013](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-013.md): behavioural and word-meaning data published as contextual show none, once context-dependent marginals are separated out. | Proposed (skimmed; a working hypothesis of its authors) |
| [THEORY-010](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-010.md): Grangier & Auffèves's "contextual objectivity" is an ontological postulate, not contextuality in either formal sense. | Proposed (the record's placement) |

**The shape.** The first two claims are the two threads, each proved in a work
the record has read. The third and fourth are how the threads relate:

- the Kochen–Specker notion sits inside the generalized one;
- the containment is strict.

Both rest on Spekkens (2005), the one source that states the link, which is
seeded and not yet read.

**Inferences.** The fifth claim notices that the threads share a
mathematical shape; it is marked as the record's inference. The sixth takes
the topic outside physics. The seventh places a sixth work, Grangier &
Auffèves, that uses the word differently.

**Relations.** The third claim extends the first two, the fourth extends the
first, and the fifth extends the first two.

## What was not claimed

- **Restricted fragments.** Spekkens's proof that preparation
  noncontextuality forces outcome determinism uses quantum theory's full
  preparation set. Whether it holds inside a stabilizer or interferometric
  fragment is open. That bears on Catani et al.'s unproved claim that its toy
  theory is noncontextual.
- **Sheaf ⇄ GPT.** Whether a sheaf-noncontextual empirical model yields a
  noncontextual model of the corresponding GPT fragment is not addressed by
  either work.
- **Representation learning and retrieval.** No held or seeded source
  connects contextuality to the kernel THEORY documents or to van Rijsbergen
  ([LIT-262](../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md)). One observation is recorded as an open question: measurements
  that are all functions of one random variable always have a global
  section. So linear probes on one fixed representation cannot be
  Kochen–Specker-contextual. Any contextuality in a learned system would
  have to come from the representation changing with the context. That is
  the record's reasoning from [LIT-016](../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md) Prop 3.1, not a published result.
- **The contextual fraction.** It would extend the first claim as a graded
  measure. It is left as a candidate until its supplementary proofs are read.

## Tag audit

Tagged:

- first: [LIT-016](../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md) and [LIT-003](../../record/literature.d/LIT-003.md);
- second, after `quantum-foundations`: [LIT-007](../../record/literature.d/LIT-007.md), [LIT-019](../../record/literature.d/LIT-019.md) and [LIT-077](../../record/literature.d/LIT-077.md).

Not tagged:

- [LIT-160](../../record/literature.d/LIT-160.md), [LIT-173](../../record/literature.d/LIT-173.md) and [LIT-208](../../record/literature.d/LIT-208.md) use "contextual" in unrelated senses.
- [LIT-054](../../record/literature.d/LIT-054.md), [LIT-062](../../record/literature.d/LIT-062.md), [LIT-073](../../record/literature.d/LIT-073.md), [LIT-081](../../record/literature.d/LIT-081.md), [LIT-086](../../record/literature.d/LIT-086.md), [LIT-121](../../record/literature.d/LIT-121.md), [LIT-018](../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), [LIT-107](../../record/literature.d/LIT-107.md) and
  [LIT-053](../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md) mention the notion at most in passing.
- [LIT-262](../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md) (van Rijsbergen): its seed gives no evidence the book treats
  contextuality. Kantor's review says it has no retrieval analogue of
  non-commuting measurements.

## To promote the Proposed claims

- A close reading of Spekkens (2005) would move the third and fourth claims.
- Kunjwal & Spekkens (2015), not held, is the noise-robust successor worth
  filing next.
- Reading Grangier's own derivations would settle the seventh.

<a id="20260927022852"></a>

## The Geometry of Information Retrieval, read

*2026-09-27 02:28:52 · curation · record*

The owner supplied the text of van Rijsbergen's *The Geometry of Information
Retrieval* ([LIT-262](../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md)): front matter, Preface, Prologue, chapters 1–6 and the
index. The appendices and the annotated bibliography were not included.

The book had been seeded that morning from the publisher's excerpts and one
review. It is now read, and it is `Active` with a `Read` note ([NOTE-239](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-239.md)).

## Two corrections to what the record said

1. **Riesz is the book's own point.** The seed attributed the
   functional-as-vector identification to Kantor's review. Chapter 6 (p. 74)
   states it, citing Riesz & Nagy: query matching is a linear functional, and
   so an inner product with a vector.

2. **The book models non-commuting measurement in retrieval.** The
   contextuality curation entry of this date reported Kantor's review as
   saying the book has no retrieval analogue of non-commuting measurements.
   That is not true of the book:
   - relevance and aboutness are explicitly allowed not to commute
     (AR ≠ RA), and the sequence A → R → A can change the second answer
     (pp. 21–22);
   - chapters 2 and 5 develop compatibility and the failure of distribution.

   What the book lacks is data showing these effects in retrieval, not the
   notion. That entry is left as written, since the journal is history, and
   this one corrects it.

## What the reading adds to the record's threads

- **The book never discusses contextuality.** It is therefore not tagged
  `contextuality`. But its order effects are exactly the question-order
  setting that Contextuality-by-Default analyses ([LIT-264](../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md), [THEORY-013](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-013.md)). That
  analysis found a Hilbert-space model of question order to predict no
  contextuality. Whether retrieval judgements show the book's order effects
  at all is untested, by the book or anyone the record holds.
- **GNS.** The book does not mention it and works in the opposite direction,
  from state to probability via Gleason. [THEORY-004](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)'s GNS link stays an
  inference.
- **The strongest parts are two chapters.** Chapter 5 proves that the
  subspace conditional is a Stalnaker conditional, equal to the Sasaki hook.
  Chapter 6 recasts standard retrieval operations as trace calculations.
  Everything else is a language offered, not a result shown.

<a id="20260927024840"></a>

## The Lattice Representation Hypothesis, re-read against the geometry of IR

*2026-09-27 02:48:40 · curation · record*

The owner allowed a work to be held in both records ([ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md)). They asked for
Xiong's *The Lattice Representation Hypothesis of Large Language Models* to
be re-read here in light of van Rijsbergen's *The Geometry of Information
Retrieval* ([LIT-262](../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md)). The anthology holds it as [ANTH-LIT-460](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-460.md).

**Reason for a second entry** ([ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) requires one). The anthology reads the
paper for concept geometry in LLMs. This record reads it as a piece of the
older mathematics of retrieval: formal concept analysis, Galois connections,
and the logic of lattices of classes. That is van Rijsbergen's second
chapter, and the anthology holds none of it.

The paper was read in full (arXiv v3, ICLR 2026, with appendices). It is
`Proposed` here with a `Read` note ([LIT-267](../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md), [NOTE-240](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-240.md)).

## What the re-reading found

- **The construction is van Rijsbergen's, with one change.** The paper's
  concept lattice is the (tr, in) Galois connection his chapter 2 builds for
  inverted files; its closed pairs are his monothetic kinds. The change: the
  object–attribute incidence is a thresholded linear functional on an
  embedding, not a given index-term incidence.
- **Theorem 1 is formal concept analysis's standard fact.** Any incidence has
  a complete concept lattice. The paper itself says the geometry plays no
  further role once the incidence is fixed.
- **Distributivity is never discussed, and it fails.** The reader's own
  checks, marked as such in the note:
  - the object-level lattice can fail distributivity (a three-object
    diagonal context gives M₃), exactly as van Rijsbergen shows for kinds;
  - the region lattice is Boolean for linearly independent directions;
  - it is non-distributive for dependent ones.
- **No projectors, no trace-rule probability, no non-commuting operations.**
  So van Rijsbergen's quantum-probabilistic layer has no counterpart here,
  and contextuality has no purchase on the text. Two further observations,
  both the reader's own:
  - the paper's soft incidence is a sign-sensitive per-attribute marginal,
    not a probability measure on the lattice;
  - its inclusion score is not reflexive.
- **The evidence.** On five WordNet domains, linear probes recover an
  incidence generated by GPT-4o at F1 69.7–83.2. No lattice law is tested.

## The anthology's entry needs correcting

Per [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) this record reports these and does not edit the anthology. I
checked the first against the paper's text; the rest are the reader's
findings.

1. **The join.** [ANTH-LIT-460](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-460.md) says the join is "the conic hull of the two
   concepts' attribute directions". Definition 7 defines it as the set union
   R(Y_A) ∪ R(Y_B), which "can be approximated by the conic hull". A union of
   cones is generally not a region of the family, so it is not a lattice
   join. The experiments use neither: they use coordinatewise min and max of
   attribute profiles.
2. **The evidence.** The attribute schema and the "ground-truth" incidence
   were generated by GPT-4o (§4), not taken from WordNet, which supplies only
   the hierarchy.
3. **The complete lattice** proved is the finite object-level concept
   lattice, not a lattice of regions.
4. **The soft version** is thresholded to a crisp incidence before any
   lattice appears. No soft lattice is proved.
5. **The canonical-form condition** is that Dc = τ is solvable. Linear
   independence of the directions is sufficient, not the condition itself.
6. **The causal inner product** appears only in the preliminaries. The
   experiments use Fisher-LDA directions on raw hidden states.

Items 1, 3 and 4 bear on [ANTH-THEORY-034](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/theory.d/THEORY-034.md)'s account, which the anthology
should re-check.

## Attention as sparse distributed memory, and ZipNN, read for this record

*2026-09-27 03:55:48 · curation · record*

The owner asked for nucleation readings of two works. Both were read in full
and both are `Active`.

## Bricken & Pehlevan, *Attention Approximates Sparse Distributed Memory*

[LIT-269](../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md), [NOTE-242](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md). Also held in the anthology as [ANTH-LIT-641](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-641.md).

**Reason for a second entry** ([ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md) requires one). The anthology reads the
paper for attention practice, mainly its QK-norm retrodiction. This record
reads it as associative memory:

- Kanerva's content-addressable retrieval;
- the cerebellar mapping;
- the SDM read as a kernel smoother, set against van Rijsbergen ([LIT-262](../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md))
  and the kernel THEORY documents.

### What the reading found

- **The paper never says "kernel", but its construction is one.** The
  weight SDM gives each stored memory is the overlap of two Hamming balls,
  which is a positive-definite kernel of distance. Locally it is approximated
  by exp(β·cos), the von Mises–Fisher kernel. Softmax attention with unit
  vectors and a fitted β is then a normalised kernel smoother over the
  memories.
- **Neuron-level SDM is linear attention with a fixed binary feature map.**
  This is the reader's observation, not the paper's.
- **The approximation holds over a narrower range than the paper claims.**
  - It holds for distances below the radius d, not up to 2d. At n = 1000
    the fit over the full range has R² ≈ 0.68.
  - The overlap is a staircase, equal at distances 2k−1 and 2k.
  - The paper's analytic β is off by about 2–2.5×, because it approximates a
    far-tail binomial with a Gaussian. The β the experiments use comes from
    regression instead.

  These are the reader's recomputations.
- **The biology is weak.** The cerebellar mapping restates Kanerva's rather
  than re-arguing it. For attention it would need about 2⁶⁴ neurons, which
  the paper itself calls implausible. How a circuit would write every token
  in one forward pass is not addressed.
- **Against van Rijsbergen.** His tr(ρP) is a broad degree-2 cosine kernel
  that ranks documents and is normalised over the query. SDM and attention
  use a sharp, tunable kernel, return a reconstructed vector rather than a
  ranking, and normalise over the stored memories. Same family, different
  job.

### The anthology's entry needs correcting

This record reports these and does not edit the anthology ([ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md)).

1. **The interpolation claim.** [ANTH-LIT-641](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-641.md) and [ANTH-THEORY-097](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/theory.d/THEORY-097.md) say the
   learned QK-norm band β ∈ [10, 25] interpolates between SDM's three
   optima. The paper claims it only for two of them, the critical-distance
   and signal-to-noise optima. I checked this against the text. Its Fig. 7
   caption says the memory-capacity optimum, β = 35.5, is "much larger than
   the largest" learned βs.
2. **The residual stream.** [ANTH-LIT-641](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-641.md) says the paper interprets "the
   residual stream" through the SDM frame. The paper never mentions it (also
   checked). Its §4 covers the feed-forward block, LayerNorm, value norms,
   multi-head attention and stacking.
3. **Where the optima come from.** [ANTH-THEORY-097](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/theory.d/THEORY-097.md) credits all three to
   Kanerva's book and his 1992 review. The paper cites Kanerva (1993) for
   two of them and derives the memory-capacity optimum itself.
4. **The GPT-2 check.** The abstract's "we confirm … in pre-trained GPT2"
   overstates Appendix A.2. GPT-2's effective β mostly lies in [3, 12],
   below the QK-norm band, and GPT-2 does not normalise its queries and keys.

## ZipNN: Lossless Compression for AI Models

[LIT-268](../../record/literature.d/LIT-268.md), [NOTE-241](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-241.md). Not held in the anthology. It is tagged
`anthology-candidate` because it is chiefly about ML practice.

### What the reading found

- **The exponent carries almost all the redundancy.**
  - About 40 of its 256 values occur, and 12 cover about 99.9% of
    parameters. The exponent compresses to about 33%, while sign and
    mantissa stay near 100%.
  - Whole models compress to about 66% (BF16), 83% (FP32) and 34–48% for
    rounded "clean" models.
  - On Llama-3.1-8B, ZipNN is 17% smaller and 62% faster than Zstd.
- **The information theory is thin.**
  - The paper never computes an entropy or compares its codes to one.
  - Its explanation of the exponent skew is asserted, not argued. The paper
    itself says "No matter the reason".
  - Part of that explanation is wrong: Adam's ε does not add noise to
    weights, and 2⁻²³ is exponent 104, not 99.
  - Its "ExaByte per year" savings claim read "per month" in v1, which the
    paper's own 6 PB/day figure rules out.
- **No bearing on the record's description-length works.** Lossless coding
  of the float format compresses how the numbers are written, not the
  function the network computes. It does not touch Kolmogorov complexity or
  MDL ([LIT-224](../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md), [LIT-225](../../record/literature.d/LIT-225.md), [LIT-238](../../record/literature.d/LIT-238.md)), or the lossy compressibility of the
  Sefidgaran bounds ([LIT-233](../../record/literature.d/LIT-233.md), [LIT-236](../../record/literature.d/LIT-236.md)).

## Quantum structure claimed in LLM language, read and rejected

*2026-09-27 04:16:24 · curation · record*

The owner asked for a nucleation reading of *Entropy* 28(6):622. It is Aerts
et al., *Identifying Quantum Structure in AI Language: Evidence for
Evolutionary Convergence of Human and Artificial Cognition*: DOI
10.3390/e28060622, arXiv 2511.21731, [LIT-270](../../record/literature.d/LIT-270.md).

**Access.** MDPI refused automated requests. The full published text was read
from Europe PMC's open-access XML. The figures (captions only), the
supplementary materials and the rows the published Table 4 omits were not
read.

**Verdict: `Rejected`.** Neither of the paper's two pieces of evidence
supports its conclusion that LLM "code is structurally quantum". The first of
the two failures is already on the record.

- **The Bell test fails on context-dependent marginals.** The paper runs its
  2011 "The Animal Acts" test on ChatGPT and Gemini and reports CHSH values
  above 2. The published v1 abstract called this "quantum entanglement"; the
  journal abstract says "non-classical probability model".

  But its own tables show outcome marginals that change with context. The
  paper's CHSH is computed as if the marginals were consistent. Under that
  confound, a value above 2 does not show that no classical model exists.

  This is exactly what the record's [THEORY-013](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-013.md) records, from [LIT-264](../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md)'s
  Contextuality-by-Default analysis of the same test design on human
  subjects. That analysis found the published human violation disappears
  once marginals are handled. The paper does not cite it.

- **The Bose–Einstein fit is a relabelled Zipf curve.** It is fitted to the
  word counts of one story that Gemini wrote after being told about the
  research. From the paper's own constants, the fitted curve is essentially a
  Zipf–Mandelbrot law. Its Maxwell–Boltzmann comparator is an exponential,
  which cannot fit word frequencies. There is no goodness-of-fit statistic.

- **An internal inconsistency, checked.** Table 3 prints E(A′,B) = +1.000,
  where the text gives 0.556. The reported CHSH of 3.09 follows from 0.556;
  the table's value gives 3.53.

**Worth noting for later.** A published comment on v1 raises the same points:
Sienicki, arXiv 2601.06104. It is not held.

## NTK of matrix product states, read and rejected

*2026-09-27 04:32:47 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-271 — Rejected: the work this entry files and places; the directive lapses when its status changes -->

The owner asked for a nucleation reading of arXiv 2111.14046, Guo & Draper,
*Neural Tangent Kernel of Matrix Product States: Convergence and
Applications* ([LIT-271](../../record/literature.d/LIT-271.md)). Neither record held it. The full 19-page v1
(the only version; no published version was found) was read, and the reading
is [NOTE-244](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-244.md).

**Verdict: `Rejected`.** The paper's one sound calculation is that, in the
sequential infinite-bond-dimension limit, the MPS NTK is
Σ_k φ(x_k)·φ(x′_k) Π_{l≠k} σ_l² φ(x_l)·φ(x′_l). That is the MPS's own GP
product kernel times the constant Σ_k σ_k⁻², which follows in a line from the
model being multilinear in its tensors. I checked that reduction when filing,
and the paper never states it. Tensor Programs II ([ANTH-LIT-557](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-557.md)) covers this
kind of architecture rigorously. The distinctive claims do not hold up:

- **The lazy-training lemma is circular.** It uses the gradient at
  initialisation for all times and bounds entries, not the kernel.
- **Positive-definiteness is not proved.** The abstract says it holds
  "without any extra assumptions of the data set". The appendix proof shows
  at most semi-definiteness, and strict definiteness fails whenever
  m > Π|s_i|, the finite feature dimension the GP theorem itself assumes.
- **"Over-fitting is naturally avoided"** contradicts the paper's own
  memorisation result.
- **Several constants are off** by factors of n or 2^{−n}.
- **There are no experiments.**

The Born-machine closed form P_x(t)=1/m−(1/m−P_x(0))e^{−4mKt/Z} is correct;
the reader checked it numerically.

**Filing choices.** It is held here, not in the anthology, because it is a
theory paper with nothing for practice to act on. Its NTK ancestry is already
in the anthology ([ANTH-LIT-360](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-360.md), [ANTH-LIT-557](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-557.md), [ANTH-LIT-558](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/literature.d/LIT-558.md)). The tags are
learning-theory, probabilistic-modeling (the GP limit and Born machines) and
mathematics. The reader proposed quantum-foundations; I dropped it, because
MPS here is a function class borrowed from physics, and nothing in the paper
is about the foundations of quantum theory. No existing nucleation work is
genuinely connected. [LIT-242](../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md) (stepwise SSL as kernel PCA) was considered and
set aside.

**Trap.** `apply_read.py`'s new-NOTE path truncates the title at its first
colon, which leaves the note's heading disagreeing with its paper's title. It
bit [LIT-270](../../record/literature.d/LIT-270.md)'s note too, and was fixed by hand both times.
