## DisCoCat, founding paper and Frobenius sequel, read

*2026-09-27 04:57:53 · curation · record*

The owner asked for a reading of arXiv 1401.5980: Kartsaklis, Sadrzadeh,
Pulman & Coecke, *Reasoning about Meaning in Natural Language with Compact
Closed Categories and Frobenius Algebras* ([LIT-272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md), [NOTE-246](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-246.md)).
While it was being read, the owner added the paper it builds on, arXiv
1003.4394: Coecke, Sadrzadeh & Clark, *Mathematical Foundations for a
Compositional Distributional Model of Meaning* ([LIT-273](../../record/literature.d/LIT-273.md), [NOTE-245](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-245.md)).
Neither record held any DisCoCat or pregroup work before. The 2014 paper is
related to the 2010 one as `extends`.

**Both are `Active`, as specifications rather than results.**

- **The 2010 paper** states no theorem and runs no experiment. Its sentence
  spaces are 1-d or 2-d truth values in a toy model, and it gives no method
  for building S or the verb tensors from data. It is still where the
  ε/η composition and the single sentence space come from. Its claim that
  the category distinguishes grammatical ambiguities fails, because the
  pregroup is posetal. Its printed similarities are unnormalised inner
  products, under its own cosine definition.
- **The 2014 paper** is the citable categorical statement of the Frobenius
  lift of verbs. Its experiments are the authors' COLING 2012 numbers,
  re-reported. I checked Table 2 against COLING 2012's Table 1 and they are
  identical. The chapter drops the COLING caveat that copy-object's lead is
  "statistically insignificant", and its abstract's "verify the theoretical
  predictions" has no prediction behind it. The best result is ρ = 0.172,
  against a human bound of 0.620.

**Where basis dependence enters.** The 2010 composition is invariant under
an orthogonal change of basis. The Frobenius copying map of 2014 is not: one
random rotation moved a sentence–subject cosine from 0.008 to −0.53. The
basis dependence belongs to the Frobenius extension, not to DisCoCat as
such. That is the point of contact with van Rijsbergen's basis-free
geometry ([LIT-262](../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md)).

**A status overridden.** The 2014 reader proposed `Superseded`, by its COLING
2012 antecedent and by the later "Frobenius anatomy" papers and Kartsaklis's
thesis. None of those is in either record, and `Superseded` names its
successor. The antecedent also lacks the functorial recasting, which is the
chapter's stated contribution. So the status is `Active`, with the overlap
stated in the status note. If COLING 2012 or the thesis is filed later, this
should be revisited.

**Tags.** The 2014 paper keeps representation-learning, because its vectors
and verb matrices are built from a corpus. The 2010 paper drops it, because
it learns nothing. Neither takes quantum-foundations: both borrow the
categorical quantum formalism and say nothing about quantum theory.

**A defect fixed in passing.** [LIT-271](../../record/literature.d/LIT-271.md) reached `main` with two `number:`
keys, a lint violation. I had hand-written `number: tmp…` into the seeded
frontmatter, and `luria concretize` then prepended the real number. `luria
new lit` writes no `number:` for a temporary code, and neither should a
hand-seeded file. The stray line is removed here, and no other document
carries a duplicate.

## Where a Hilbert space gets its basis: Carroll connected, THEORY drafted

*2026-09-27 06:11:49 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-017 — Proposed: the document this entry files; the directive lapses when its status changes -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-004 — Proposed: named as the representation-learning instance; the directive lapses when its status changes -->

The owner asked for a reading of arXiv 2103.09780. It is Carroll, *Reality as
a Vector in Hilbert Space*, which the record already held as [LIT-123](../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md), read
in full the day before ([NOTE-134](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-134.md), `Active`). A second reading would have
added nothing. What had changed was the record around it: van Rijsbergen,
the two DisCoCat papers and the Riesz/GNS kernel thread were all filed after
[NOTE-134](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-134.md) was written. On the owner's go-ahead, this contribution does two
things.

**[NOTE-134](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-134.md) gains a connections paragraph (version 3).** The reading itself is
unchanged. Its "Bearing on the record" line saying no THEORY depended on the
paper is updated.

**[THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) is new, `Proposed`.** It says that in a Hilbert-space model
only unitarily invariant structure is intrinsic, and that the record's
Hilbert-space works differ in where they get a basis or factorisation. There
are four answers:

- **Carroll** takes it from the dynamics.
- **Van Rijsbergen** takes it from the observable.
- **DisCoCat 2010** needs none; its composition is orthogonally covariant.
- **Kartsaklis et al. 2014** stipulates a corpus basis.

[THEORY-004](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) is the same point for learned representations, so the new document
`extends` it. Two inferences are marked as the document's own, not the
sources':

- **Contextuality needs more than one basis**, so a single-stipulated-basis
  model such as [LIT-272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md)'s cannot be contextual.
- **Distributive, Boolean concept structure is evidence that a basis was
  chosen.**

**Why `Proposed`.** The piece that would turn "basis", "Frobenius algebra"
and "classical data" from analogies into one notion is Coecke, Pavlovic &
Vicary's theorem. That theorem is cited by [LIT-272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md) and not held here. So the
`promote_when` asks for that paper to be filed and read, and for a check that
each placement in the table rests on something measured or proved, not
inferred. It also names what would refute the account.

**Checked while writing.** A first draft said [LIT-272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md)'s basis-dependent model
"scores as well as its invariant rivals". It doesn't have invariant rivals in
that sense. Kron and Multp are elementwise too, so basis-dependent, and the
only rotation-invariant baseline, additive, scores lowest (ρ = 0.050 against
0.163–0.172). The caveat now says so. The pattern is worth noting: on that one
task, the basis-dependent models lead.

**Candidate follow-up.** Filing Coecke, Pavlovic & Vicary (arXiv 0810.0812)
would let this THEORY be promoted. It would also give [LIT-272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md)'s
Frobenius-algebra claims ([NOTE-246](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-246.md), C3) a source in the record rather than a
citation.

## Coecke, Pavlovic & Vicary read; THEORY-017 restated, still Proposed

*2026-09-27 06:26:32 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-017 — Proposed: the account this entry revises; the directive lapses when its status changes -->

The owner asked for arXiv 0810.0812 next: Coecke, Pavlovic & Vicary, *A New
Description of Orthogonal Bases* (MSCS 23(3), 2013). [THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md)'s
`promote_when` had named it. It is filed as [LIT-274](../../record/literature.d/LIT-274.md), read in full as
[NOTE-247](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-247.md), and `Active`.

**What it proves.**

- **Thm 5.1.** In FdHilb, commutative †-Frobenius algebras are in bijection
  with *orthogonal* bases, the basis being the vectors the comultiplication
  copies. The bijection is of sets, for each fixed space.
- **§6.** The special ones are exactly the orthonormal bases, with the
  vectors fixed exactly, phases included.
- **Corollaries 7.1–7.2.** These give categorical equivalences with finite
  sets labelled by positive reals, and with FinSet.
- **The proof.** Its key step rests on the cited spectral theorem for
  finite-dimensional commutative C*-algebras.
- **Language and scope.** The paper says "classical data", never "classical
  structure". It says nothing about infinite dimensions, distributions,
  contextuality or projection lattices.

**What changed in [THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md).** It now states the correspondence as proved:
orthogonal bases for commutative †-Frobenius algebras, orthonormal bases for
special ones. It also gains a caveat that the correspondence holds on complex
spaces only.

- **The real-space counterexample.** The reader found it, and I checked it
  numerically: on ℝ², the complex numbers with multiplication scaled by
  1/√2 form a commutative special †-Frobenius algebra with no nonzero
  copyable vector. The associativity, Frobenius, special and commutativity
  laws all hold, and the copy residual shrinks only as the vector goes to
  zero.
- **What it means for the table.** [LIT-273](../../record/literature.d/LIT-273.md), [LIT-272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md) and [THEORY-004](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) work over
  the reals. A basis there still induces a Frobenius algebra, which is all
  [LIT-272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md) uses, so the table's placements stand. But "basis" and "Frobenius
  algebra" are one notion only in the complex case.

**Why it stays `Proposed`.** The first `promote_when` condition is met. The
second is not. Two placements rest on the readers' own numerical checks,
not on the papers' claims: [LIT-273](../../record/literature.d/LIT-273.md)'s orthogonal covariance and [LIT-272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md)'s
rotation sensitivity. The `promote_when` now says so. Promoting on the
strength of what the readers computed would be exactly the move the field
exists to prevent.

**[NOTE-246](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-246.md) corrected (version bump).** Two sentences overstated this paper.
The spider normal form is not in it, though [LIT-272](../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md) cites it for that. And
the basis correspondence needs † and a complex Hilbert space. Its claims
table's C3 was accurate and is unchanged.

**Candidate follow-up, not filed.** For infinite dimensions, the reader found
by search, but did not read, Abramsky & Heunen (arXiv 1011.6123). That is
where [THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md)'s finite-dimensional boundary would be tested.

## Abramsky & Heunen read; THEORY-017's finite-dimensional caveat narrowed

*2026-09-27 06:43:22 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-017 — Proposed: the account this entry revises; the directive lapses when its status changes -->

The owner asked for arXiv 1011.6123: Abramsky & Heunen, *H\*-algebras and
nonunital Frobenius algebras* (AMS PSAPM 71, 2012). The previous entry had
named it as the test of [THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md)'s finite-dimensional boundary. It is
filed as [LIT-275](../../record/literature.d/LIT-275.md), read in full as [NOTE-248](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-248.md) (arXiv v3, the final
version), `Active`, and it `extends` [LIT-274](../../record/literature.d/LIT-274.md).

**Checked against the text when filing:** Lemma 3, Theorem 22,
Proposition 23 and Theorem 35 read as the reader reported.

**What it proves.**

- **Lemma 3.** A unital Frobenius algebra exists in Hilb only in finite
  dimension.
- **Theorem 22.** Without the unit, a commutative special †-Frobenius
  algebra on a complex Hilbert space of any dimension is induced by an
  orthonormal basis exactly when it satisfies Ambrose's H\*-axiom,
  equivalently when it is semisimple, or a directed colimit of finite unital
  ones. It adds an approximate-identity form for separable spaces.
- **Proposition 23.** It leaves open whether the axiom is automatic, i.e.
  whether a radical part can exist.
- **Tools.** It uses Gelfand theory and Ambrose, not GNS or C\*-algebras.
- **Relations.** In categories of relations the axiom is proved, for
  quantale-valued relations only under Theorem 35's hypothesis q² = 1 ⇒
  q = 1. The abstract's "always coincide" overstates this.

**[THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) (version 3).** The "stays finite-dimensional" caveat is
narrowed. A discrete basis is extra structure supplied as an algebra on the
space in any dimension. Only continuous observables, which the paper defers,
remain outside, and that is where Carroll's and the GNS strand's "an algebra
of observables must be supplied" applies. The real-scalar caveat now holds
in every dimension: the reader found that ℂ regarded as a real algebra
satisfies the H\*-axiom and has no copyable vectors. I checked the other
axioms numerically in the previous contribution; the H\*-axiom check is the
reader's. The document stays `Proposed`, on the same remaining
`promote_when` condition.

**Small corrections recorded in the NOTE.** The paper's "Theorem 1
[CPV09]" is Coecke, Pavlovic & Vicary's §6 (special/orthonormal) form, not
their Theorem 5.1 (orthogonal). The orthogonal case appears here only as a
sketch in a footnote.

**Candidate follow-up, not filed.** Poinsot, *Hilbertian Frobenius algebras*
(arXiv 2003.04149, 2020). By its abstract, which is all the reader saw, every

## Measurement as sheafification, read and rejected

*2026-09-27 07:26:15 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-276 — Rejected: the work this entry files and places; the directive lapses when its status changes -->

The owner asked for arXiv 2512.12249 v2: Ghose, *Measurement as
Sheafification: Context, Logic, and Truth after Quantum Mechanics*. It is
filed as [LIT-276](../../record/literature.d/LIT-276.md), read in full as [NOTE-249](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md), `Rejected`. The
reader read v2 and compared it word by word with v1. No journal version was
found.

**Verdict.** It is an interpretive essay with no theorem, model or
computation of its own. Its correct formal core is Abramsky–Brandenburger's
global-section criterion, which the record holds first-hand as [LIT-016](../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md) and
[THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md). Each of its three additions is asserted without a construction,
or is wrong as stated:

- **"Measurement is sheafification."** It gives no site, no topology and no
  sheafified presheaf. Sheaf toposes are not Boolean in general (Sh(ℝ) is
  not). And classical probability distributions do not form a sheaf, since
  the marginal problem breaks gluing.
- **The seven-valued Ghose–Patra logic as "a finite Heyting algebra".** It
  gives no order and no operations. The structure its Appendix B implies is
  not a lattice, and completing it gives the Boolean algebra 2³.
- **The σ–λ dynamics.** λ(σ) is never specified, nothing is computed, and
  there is no prediction.

**v2's added Čech obstruction is always zero.** I checked this against the
text when filing. The appendix defines the class as [δs] for a 0-cochain s.
That is the class of a coboundary, so it vanishes for every s, and "[δs] ≠ 0"
can never hold. The paragraph that follows describes Abramsky, Mansfield &
Barbosa's actual construction correctly, but only by citation.

**Beyond its comment, v2 also:**

- deletes v1's introduction, leaving refs [1]–[8] uncited;
- deletes v1's only empirical claim, the micellar-surfactant one;
- adds a quantum-gravity paragraph.

**Bearing.** It supports no THEORY. Its slogan "Boolean needs a sheaf"
resembles [THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md)'s inference "Boolean structure needs a basis", and the
NOTE warns against reading it as support. The slogan is false as stated,
and [THEORY-017](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md)'s inference rests on different grounds.

**Candidate follow-up, not filed.** Abramsky, Mansfield & Barbosa's
cohomology of contextuality is the correct version of what v2's appendix
attempts, and neither record holds it. Filing it would give [THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md) and
[LIT-265](../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md) their cohomological companion.

## Cohomology of contextuality read; Ghose note corrected, THEORY-012 bounded

*2026-09-27 07:38:16 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-276 — Rejected: the Ghose paper whose reading this entry corrects; the directive lapses when its status changes -->

The owner asked for Abramsky, Mansfield & Barbosa's cohomology of
contextuality, the follow-up the Ghose entry named. It is arXiv 1111.3620,
*The Cohomology of Non-Locality and Contextuality* (QPL 2011, EPTCS 95,
2012). It is filed as [LIT-277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md) and read in full as [NOTE-250](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-250.md) (v2,
compared with v1 word by word). It is `Active`, and it `extends` [LIT-016](../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md).

**What it shows.**

- **The obstruction.** For a section s of context C₁, the obstruction γ(s)
  is the class of δ⁰(s, s₂, …, sₙ) in the relative group Ȟ¹(𝒰, F_{C̄₁}),
  where F is the presheaf of ℤ-combinations of support sections.
- **What vanishing means.** γ(s) = 0 iff s extends to a compatible family of
  ℤ-combinations (Prop 4.2), which need not be a global section. So a
  non-vanishing class witnesses possibilistic or strong contextuality, and
  only in one direction: it is sufficient, not necessary.
- **Where it works.** γ is non-zero for the PR box, GHZ, the 18-vector
  Kochen–Specker set and Peres–Mermin.
- **Where it fails.** γ vanishes on all of Hardy's model, and on 9 of 15
  sections of a strongly contextual Kochen–Specker cover.

The reader recomputed every example over ℤ and ℤ/2.

**A v1 error, verified.** v1's "strongly contextual" false-positive cover,
{A,B,C}, {A,D,E}, {B,D,E}, {A,D,F}, {A,E,G}, is not strongly contextual. I
enumerated it when filing: it has exactly two global Kochen–Specker
assignments. v2 silently replaced it.

**[NOTE-249](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md) corrected (Ghose).** Its description of this construction was
written from general knowledge. "Not the class of a 0-coboundary" was wrong
as worded: γ(s) is a coboundary's class, taken relative to C₁ and built from
data that are not cochains of the relative presheaf. The note now says what
Ghose's [δs] drops (the relativisation, the anchoring and the cover), and
why that makes it vanish. The verdict on Ghose is unchanged.

**[THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md) bounded (version bump).** Its "does not say" gains a line: the
cohomological witness is a computable relaxation of the exact
global-section criterion, not an equivalent. The claim itself is unchanged.

**Candidate follow-ups, existence checked only.**

- Abramsky, Barbosa, Kishida, Lal & Mansfield, *Contextuality, Cohomology
  and Paradox* (CSL 2015, arXiv 1502.03097).
- Carù (arXiv 1701.00656 and 1807.04203).
- Okay, Roberts, Bartlett & Raussendorf, *Topological proofs of
  contextuality* (arXiv 1701.01888).

## Contextuality, Cohomology and Paradox read; THEORY-012's cohomology line refined

*2026-09-27 08:14:56 · curation · record*

The owner asked for *Contextuality, Cohomology and Paradox*: Abramsky,
Barbosa, Kishida, Lal & Mansfield, arXiv 1502.03097, CSL 2015. It is filed
as [LIT-278](../../record/literature.d/LIT-278.md) and read in full as [NOTE-251](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-251.md). That covers v2, which
matches the published LIPIcs text, and v1, which holds the only proof of
Prop 16. It is `Active`, and it `extends` [LIT-277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md).

**What it proves.**

- **Theorem 21.** For a connected cover, AvN_R(S) ⇒ SC(Aff S) ⇒ CSC_R(S) ⇒
  CSC_ℤ(S) ⇒ SC(S). So a model with an All-vs-Nothing argument, over any
  commutative ring, is strongly contextual, and its cohomological
  obstruction is non-zero on every section.
- **Theorem 4.** Stabiliser states of n-qubit "AvN triples" of Paulis supply
  such models (qubits only).
- **GHZ(3).** §4.1 is a complete hand proof, the case [NOTE-016](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-016.md) had recorded
  as only sketched.

**The paradox half proves little.**

- **One exact case.** The length-4 Liar cycle is the PR box.
- **The rest is analogy.** The cohomology of paradox is deferred.
- **Scope of the encoding.** It fails for the classic Liar (N = 1) and for
  N = 2. For N ≥ 3 the Liar cycles are All-vs-Nothing over ℤ₂; I checked
  that when filing. The strong contextuality then follows from Theorem 21,
  though the paper doesn't say so.

**[NOTE-250](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-250.md)'s gaps are not closed.** The reader found that Hardy's affine
closure is the whole event sheaf, so no All-vs-Nothing argument reaches
Hardy. By Theorem 21, the §8 strongly contextual cover of [LIT-277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md) has no
All-vs-Nothing argument over any ring. The paper mentions neither, and v2
deletes v1's sentence about Hardy.

**[THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md) (version bump).** Its cohomology line now says where the
witness *is* complete: on All-vs-Nothing models. It also says that both of
[LIT-277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md)'s documented failures lie outside that class. The derivation for
covers failing the GCD condition is marked as the reader's own. The claim
is unchanged.

**Silent corrections between versions.**

- v2 corrects v1's GHZ parity equations without comment.
- v2 adds "all known quantum examples of strong contextuality are of AvN
  type" with no citation.

**Follow-up.** By its abstract (unread), Carù's arXiv 1701.00656 disproves
[LIT-277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md)'s Conjecture 8.1. It is now the most direct next reading on this

## Carù read: the cohomology conjecture is false; THEORY-012 updated

*2026-09-27 08:29:06 · curation · record*

The owner asked for arXiv 1701.00656: Carù, *On the Cohomology of
Contextuality* (QPL 2016, EPTCS 236). It is filed as [LIT-279](../../record/literature.d/LIT-279.md) and read
in full as [NOTE-252](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-252.md) (v1, the only version). It is `Active`, and it
`corrects` [LIT-277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md).

**The counterexample holds.**

- **The model.** It sits on the two-party, two-setting, four-outcome Bell
  cover.
- **Checks.** The reader reproduced [NOTE-250](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-250.md)'s counts first, as a
  calibration: Hardy 13/13, PR box 0/8, AMB §8 cover 9/15. Then, with exact
  ℤ and ℤ/2 linear algebra, the reader confirmed that the model is strongly
  contextual and that γ = 0 on all 22 sections. I checked the strong
  contextuality by hand when filing; the γ computation is the reader's.
- **Beyond the paper.**
  - The reader found, by linear programming, a no-signalling probability
    model with this support.
  - The model has no All-vs-Nothing argument. That follows from [LIT-278](../../record/literature.d/LIT-278.md)'s
    Theorem 21 by contraposition, and the reader also checked it directly
    over ℤ₄.

**Scope of the refutation.** It refutes Conjecture 8.1 for symmetry of the
cover, and for "no measurement confined to one context". It does not touch
covers whose contexts pairwise intersect (AMB's own §8 cover is one), or
symmetric models: this model has 2 automorphisms, against the PR box's 16.

**The rest of the paper is weaker.**

- **The hierarchy collapses.** The higher-obstruction hierarchy (Prop 5.5)
  is empty above level 0 for every no-signalling model, by the paper's own
  Prop 5.6. So the abstract's "hierarchy of levels of contextuality" is the
  one level AMB already had.
- **Prop 6.1 is false in its "only if" direction.** The PR box is a
  counterexample.
- **No positive completeness result.**

It closes neither the Hardy gap nor the §8 cover.

**[THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md) (version bump).** Its cohomology line records the refutation
and the open cases. The claim itself is unchanged.

**Follow-up, existence only.** Carù, arXiv 1807.04203, *Towards a complete
cohomology invariant*, is the natural next reading on this line.

## Carù 2018 read: complete on cycles, conjecture refuted

*2026-09-27 16:16:44 · curation · record*

The owner asked for arXiv 1807.04203: Carù, *Towards a complete cohomology
invariant for non-locality and contextuality*. It is filed as [LIT-280](../../record/literature.d/LIT-280.md)
and read in full as [NOTE-253](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-253.md) (v1, the only version, 46 pp.). It is
`Active`, and it `extends` [LIT-279](../../record/literature.d/LIT-279.md). No published version was found. The
author's 2019 DPhil thesis was not obtained, so whether it repairs §8 is
unverified.

**What holds: Theorem 7.7.** On cyclic covers, ℤ/2 cohomology of the
(N−1)-th iterated joint model is exact for logical and strong
contextuality. The reader implemented the construction and checked it on
659 random contextual cycle models. It detects:

- Carù 2017's (2,2,4) model at level 3, on 22 of 22 sections;
- Hardy's one contextual section at level 3.

The paper claims both, and the computation confirms them. So both of the
record's gaps on cycles are closed.

**What fails.**

- **Conjecture 9.1 is refuted.** Under the paper's Definition 7.1, [LIT-277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md)'s
  §8 cover is undetected at every level. The reader built the lifted
  witness family explicitly up to level 4, which has 1350 contexts. I re-ran
  the reader's level-1 witness script when filing, and its independent
  compatibility check passes.
- **Prop 8.2 is false** on the paper's own Table 5 model.
- **The paper's recount of the §8 cover is wrong** (4/15 against the correct
  9/15).
- **The worked examples use a weaker, context-wise definition** than the
  theorems. That weaker version detects the §8 cover at level 2; that
  finding is the reader's.
- **The abstract's "vast majority of empirical models"** is established only
  for cycles.
- **Cost** is never analysed. The iterated objects grow exponentially:
  5, 10, 30, 150, 1350 contexts on the §8 cover.

**[THEORY-012](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md) (version bump).** Its cohomology line records the partial
repair on cycles and the refutation off them, and "still open" is
restated. The claim itself is unchanged.

**The line so far.**

- [LIT-277](../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md): the witness.
- [LIT-278](../../record/literature.d/LIT-278.md): complete on All-vs-Nothing models.
- [LIT-279](../../record/literature.d/LIT-279.md): incomplete on symmetric covers.
- [LIT-280](../../record/literature.d/LIT-280.md): complete on cycles, with the general conjecture false.

## Sen's capability approach, assembled from nine texts

*2026-09-28 02:56:43 · curation · record*

The owner asked for Amartya Sen's ideas to be represented, and suggested
assembling the capability approach from shorter texts and reviews rather
than reading *The Idea of Justice* (2009) in full. Nothing by or about Sen
was held before this entry.

A scoping pass checked what was legitimately and fully reachable. Nine texts
were then read in full, by four readers working in parallel, and each is
filed `Active` with a `Read` NOTE.

| Role | Work | LIT | NOTE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sen, core statement | *Equality of What?* (Tanner Lecture, 1979) | [LIT-289](../../record/literature.d/LIT-289.md) | [NOTE-258](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-258.md) |
| Sen, social-choice grounding | *The Possibility of Social Choice* (Nobel lecture, 1998) | [LIT-282](../../record/literature.d/LIT-282.md) | [NOTE-263](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-263.md) |
| Sen, formal result | *The Impossibility of a Paretian Liberal* (JPE 1970) | [LIT-285](../../record/literature.d/LIT-285.md) | [NOTE-255](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-255.md) |
| Overview | Robeyns & Byskov, SEP *The Capability Approach* (2011; 2025 revision read) | [LIT-283](../../record/literature.d/LIT-283.md) | [NOTE-260](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-260.md) |
| Overview | Wells, IEP *Sen's Capability Approach* (2012) | [LIT-284](../../record/literature.d/LIT-284.md) | [NOTE-257](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-257.md) |
| Synthesis | Robeyns, *Wellbeing, Freedom and Social Justice* (2017) | [LIT-287](../../record/literature.d/LIT-287.md) | [NOTE-259](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-259.md) |
| Critique, the list | Nussbaum, *Capabilities as Fundamental Entitlements* (2003) | [LIT-288](../../record/literature.d/LIT-288.md) | [NOTE-256](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-256.md) |
| Critique, justice method | Valentini, *A Paradigm Shift in Theorizing about Justice?* (2010/2011) | [LIT-290](../../record/literature.d/LIT-290.md) | [NOTE-262](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-262.md) |
| The 2009 book, indexed | Zwolinski, review of *The Idea of Justice* (2010) | [LIT-286](../../record/literature.d/LIT-286.md) | [NOTE-261](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-261.md) |

The relations added are: the Nobel lecture `extends` the 1970 paper, and
both Nussbaum and Robeyns `extend` the 1979 lecture.

## The account, piece by piece, and where each piece comes from

Each claim below is marked **first-hand** (read in a Sen text here) or
**second-hand** (reported by a secondary source, which is named).

1. **The negative argument (first-hand, 1979).** Three measures of advantage
   are each insufficient, even for the needs-based part of equality:
   - *utilitarian equality* (equal marginal utility), because
     sum-maximisation gives the less efficient converter of income into
     utility *less* income, pp. 203–204;
   - *total-utility equality*, completed as leximin, because a contented
     disabled person with low aspirations shows no utility deficit,
     pp. 217–218;
   - *Rawls's primary goods*, which are "fetishist" because they take goods
     "as the embodiment of advantage, rather than taking advantage to be a
     relationship between persons and goods", p. 216.

   The disabled person's claim is tracked by none of them.
2. **The positive proposal (first-hand, 1979).** "Basic capability
   equality", meaning "a person being able to do certain basic things"
   (p. 218). Sen offers it only as "a partial guide" to the equality part of
   morality, and says the negative thesis stands without it (p. 220). The
   index of capability bundles yields only a *partial ordering*, completed
   by culture-dependent conventions (p. 219).

   The 1979 text never uses "functioning", "capability set", "agency" or
   "freedom". Accounts that credit it with the full later vocabulary, or
   with *replacing* utility and primary goods, read later Sen back into it.
   Robeyns does this (p. 76 n. 39; [NOTE-259](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-259.md)), and so does the IEP entry
   in places.
3. **The mature vocabulary (second-hand).**
   - Functionings are achieved beings and doings; capabilities are the
     real opportunities to achieve them; the capability set is the menu
     (per the SEP and the IEP).
   - Conversion factors are why equal resources yield unequal capabilities
     (per all three secondary sources).
   - Adaptive preferences are why utility misleads (per the IEP, quoting
     *Commodities and Capabilities*).
   - Well-being freedom is distinguished from agency freedom, and freedom
     from achievement. This is attributed to the Dewey Lectures (1985) by
     the SEP (§2.5) alone; the IEP never mentions it. No Sen text for it
     was reachable.
4. **The social-choice grounding (first-hand, 1998).**
   - *What escapes Arrow is interpersonal comparability.* Even ordinal
     comparisons break the exact impossibility, and partial comparability
     often suffices. Capabilities enter only as *one* candidate answer to
     "comparison of what?", which Sen declines to make exclusive.
   - *The liberal paradox is different.* Sen proved it in 1970, and the
     reader checked the proof. It is explicitly *not* resolved by
     comparability (p. 199).
   - *A correction to the scoping report.* It ran these steps together.
5. **The "no fixed list" stance and public reasoning (second-hand).** Sen
   refuses "one pre-determined canonical list" (SEP §3.3, quoting "Human
   Rights and Capabilities" 2005, p. 158). The two overviews disagree about
   what replaces the list:
   - the IEP credits Sen with a social-choice procedure of "intersection" and
     "ranges of weights" (§3b);
   - the SEP says he has "never explained in detail" how selection should
     work (§3.3).
6. **Justice (second-hand, via two readers of the 2009 book).**
   - *Comparative, not transcendental.* Sen argues for a comparative,
     "realization-focused" approach against "transcendental
     institutionalism" (Valentini; Zwolinski).
   - *Positional objectivity* and the impartial spectator (Zwolinski).
   - *Freedom* is "an inescapably plural idea" (Zwolinski, IoJ p. 305).
   - *Human rights* whose realisation need not be the state's task
     (Zwolinski, IoJ p. 364).

   The two readers agree on what the book says and disagree on whether it
   matters. The SEP adds that the capability approach is not itself a theory
   of justice (§4). The IEP calls Sen a "comprehensive consequentialist",
   and the SEP calls that contested.

## The critiques as the record now holds them

- **Nussbaum: the list and the threshold.** The approach yields no theory
  of justice without a definite, revisable list of central capabilities,
  owed up to a threshold. She gives ten. "Freedom" is not a general good,
  since some freedoms are trivial or unjust. She endorses Sen's arguments
  against GNP, utility and resources. Her threshold is named but not
  specified in this paper, and Sen's side appears only as her reports of
  his oral remarks.
- **Valentini: method.** Each of Sen's complaints against transcendental
  theory either misreads Rawls or is true but inconsequential. "If there are
  transcendental institutionalists, Rawls is not one of them." She says
  nothing about capabilities.
- **Robeyns: the modular reply.** The core is eight "A-module" commitments;
  particular theories fill seven compulsory-but-open modules. She uses this
  to argue that the standard critiques (no list, individualism, power,
  liberalism) hit particular capability theories, not the approach. The
  approach is committed to ethical, not ontological, individualism. She is
  an advocate and Sen's former student; read her as a reconstruction that
  generalises Sen, including dropping his "reason to value" clause.
- **Pogge's resourcist critique is not represented.** None of the nine texts
  states his argument. The scoping report expected Robeyns 2017 and the SEP
  to carry it, and both readers found that neither does. Pogge 2002 itself
  is paywalled.

## Errors found in the secondary sources (checked against Sen 1979)

- **The SEP inverts Sen's pleasure-wizard.** In Sen the pleasure-wizard is
  person B, not the disabled person A (p. 203). I checked this against the
  text when filing. The SEP also merges his argument against utilitarianism
  with his separate argument against total-utility equality (§§1.1, 2.6).
- **Robeyns over-attributes to the 1979 lecture.**
  - She has it argue that almost any theory of justice is egalitarian in some
    space (p. 94 n. 2). The lecture makes no such argument; the reader
    thinks the thesis is from *Inequality Reexamined* (1992), unverified.
  - She counts it as endorsing her whole A-module (p. 76 n. 39).
- **The IEP** is internally inconsistent on when the approach began ("1980s"
  against 1979), and drops Sen's condition from the utilitarian argument.

## What is missing, and why

**Sen's own statements.** None of these is reachable legitimately, and all
are represented only second-hand through the SEP and the IEP:

- the Dewey Lectures (1985), the source for agency freedom;
- *Capability and Well-Being* (1993);
- *Capabilities, Lists, and Public Reason* (2004);
- *Elements of a Theory of Human Rights* (2004);
- *Human Rights and Capabilities* (2005);
- *Development as Capability Expansion* (1989).

**Critics.** Pogge (2002) and Anderson (1999) are also unreachable.

**Blocked hosts.** Sen's Harvard page, the Tanner Lectures site, PhilArchive
and Open Book Publishers' own site refused automated requests. The owner may
be able to fetch copies in a browser. The Dewey Lectures and the 2004
*Lists* paper would most improve the account.

**Dating conventions.**

- Valentini's `published:` is the November 2010 working paper, which is her
  first appearance ([ADR-002](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-002.md)).
- Zwolinski's issue date is inferred and unverified.
- Nussbaum was read from her own preprint, so her page numbers are not the
  journal's.

**Existing record links.**

- [LIT-202](../../record/literature.d/LIT-202.md) (preference formation) is cited for adaptive preferences, but only
  thematically: it cites Elster and Khader, not Sen.
- [LIT-146](../../record/literature.d/LIT-146.md) treats Nussbaum's capabilities as a value theory for animals.

No THEORY document was filed. The candidate claim — that Arrow is escaped by
comparability, while the Paretian-liberal paradox is not — rests for its
Arrow half on Sen's 1970 book, which is not held.

## Frankfurt's account of higher-order volitions, assembled from seven texts

*2026-09-29 20:09:53 · curation · record*

The owner asked for Harry Frankfurt's account of higher-order volitions to
be represented. Nothing on it was held before this entry. A scoping pass
found that the core texts are all out of legitimate reach:

- Frankfurt's 1969–1994 papers, including "Freedom of the Will and the
  Concept of a Person" (1971);
- Watson's "Free Agency" (1975);
- Bratman's papers.

The copies of the 1971 paper found on course sites were not used. Seven texts
were read in full and each is filed `Active` with a `Read` NOTE:

| Role | Work | LIT | NOTE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frankfurt, first-hand (late view) | Tanner Lectures, *Taking Ourselves Seriously* / *Getting It Right* (2004) | [LIT-293](../../record/literature.d/LIT-293.md) | [NOTE-264](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-264.md) |
| The 1971 apparatus and the replies | McKenna & Coates, SEP *Compatibilism* (2004; 2024 revision read) | [LIT-291](../../record/literature.d/LIT-291.md) | [NOTE-270](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-270.md) |
| Overview of autonomy | Buss & Westlund, SEP *Personal Autonomy* (2002; 2018 revision read) | [LIT-296](../../record/literature.d/LIT-296.md) | [NOTE-267](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-267.md) |
| Overview of autonomy | Dryden, IEP *Autonomy* (2010) | [LIT-297](../../record/literature.d/LIT-297.md) | [NOTE-266](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-266.md) |
| Critique of the hierarchy | Velleman, *What Happens When Someone Acts?* (1992) | [LIT-295](../../record/literature.d/LIT-295.md) | [NOTE-265](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-265.md) |
| Critique of the late view | Velleman, *Identification and Identity* (2002) | [LIT-292](../../record/literature.d/LIT-292.md) | [NOTE-268](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-268.md) |
| The 1969 cases | Robb, SEP *Moral Responsibility and the Principle of Alternative Possibilities* (2020) | [LIT-294](../../record/literature.d/LIT-294.md) | [NOTE-269](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-269.md) |

## The account, and where each piece comes from

Each claim below is marked **first-hand** (read in Frankfurt here) or
**second-hand**, with the source named.

1. **The 1971 hierarchy (second-hand, SEP *Compatibilism* §4.2.1).**
   - First-order desires are for actions; second-order desires are
     desires about one's desires.
   - The *will* is the "effective first-order desire", the one that moves
     one "all the way to action".
   - A mere second-order desire (the therapist who wants to know what
     craving is like) differs from a *second-order volition*, a desire that
     a given desire be one's will.
   - The unwilling addict has a second-order volition against the craving
     that moves him. The willing addict endorses it.
   - The formula for free will: "One acts of her own free will if and only
     if her action issues from the will she wants". I checked the wording
     against the entry when filing.
   - Page references are to the Watson (ed.) 1982 reprint.
2. **Wantons and persons (second-hand, and only in older revisions).**
   - Only persons have second-order volitions. Wantons are "passive
     bystanders to their wills". "The wanton is not a person, and so is not
     a candidate for freely willed action."
   - This is in the SEP *Compatibilism* revisions of 2004–2015 only (e.g.
     the Fall 2019 archive edition). The 26 Nov 2019 revision dropped it.
   - None of the other six texts states it, and the Tanner Lectures
     mention only "wantonly unreflective" animals and small children
     (p. 172).
3. **Freedom of action vs freedom of the will (first-hand, Tanner p. 177).**
   Frankfurt restates the distinction and his compatibilism (p. 178). No
   secondary source in the batch does.
4. **The mature view (first-hand, Tanner Lectures).** I checked the
   quotations against the lecture PDF.
   - *Identification* is largely a default "willing acceptance", "whether
     with a welcoming approval, or in weary resignation".
   - *Free will* is "a certain volitional unanimity": the governing desire
     agrees "with a higher-order volition" and conflicts with no desire "at
     any higher order". That is wholeheartedness.
   - *Caring* is wanting to go on wanting.
   - *Love* is volitional. Its necessities "may be irresistible, but they
     are not coercive". It is "the only legitimate authority" for our
     normative attitudes.
   - The lectures do not use the terms "second-order desire" or
     "second-order volition", do not discuss the regress, and never name
     Watson. The case for love's authority rests on the stipulation that
     lovers are never ambivalent.
5. **The regress and Watson (second-hand, and the sources disagree).**
   - The IEP and SEP *Compatibilism* credit Watson (1975) with the
     authority/regress objection. SEP *Personal Autonomy* states the regress
     as its own argument, credits it to nobody, and files Watson 1975 as a
     *rival* (valuational) account.
   - Velleman (1992) reports the regress as Watson's objection, which
     Frankfurt conceded.
   - None of the sources reports Watson's valuing-versus-desiring
     distinction in any detail.
6. **Frankfurt's replies (second-hand, dated inconsistently).**
   - *Decisive commitment:* the IEP and Velleman place its germ in 1971
     itself; SEP *Compatibilism* says 1971 "rested solely" on higher-order
     volition.
   - *Wholeheartedness:* the IEP dates it to 1987, SEP *Compatibilism* to
     1994.
   - *Satisfaction (1992):* only SEP *Personal Autonomy*, n. 1, mentions it.
   - *Manipulation:* SEP *Compatibilism* quotes Frankfurt (2002, p. 27)
     accepting that a character given by a manipulator still leaves a person
     responsible.
   - *Resignation:* the resigned willing addict is excluded by the 1994
     amendment according to SEP *Compatibilism*, but Frankfurt's own 2004
     text counts acceptance "in weary resignation" as identification.
7. **Critiques.**
   - *Velleman 1992:* on the "standard story" of action the agent drops
     out. Any state defined without the agent's participation (second-order
     desires, Watson's values, decisive commitments) can be disowned, and
     any state defined to include it presupposes what it was meant to
     explain. His alternative: the agent is whatever plays the agent's
     functional role, the desire to act in accordance with reasons.
   - *Velleman 2002:* this targets the late view. An essence made of
     volitional necessities would yield authenticity, not autonomy.
     Wholeheartedness is a defensive ideal (the Rat Man). Frankfurt's
     "Reply to J. David Velleman" in the same volume was not obtained.
   - *Manipulation* and *mesh* objections: per SEP *Compatibilism* and
     *Personal Autonomy*.
   - *Bratman's self-governing policies* (2007): per SEP *Compatibilism*
     only. Bratman 1996 and 2004 are reported by no source.
8. **Frankfurt cases (1969; second-hand, Robb).** These cases are the
   strongest attack on the principle that responsibility requires being
   able to do otherwise, and there is "not much consensus". The 1969 case
   appears only in Fischer's retelling. The bridge to the hierarchy (§5.1)
   is that identification or endorsement is one of two compatibilist
   accounts of responsibility after Frankfurt cases.

## Gaps, and what would fill them

- **Frankfurt 1971, 1976, 1987, 1992 and 1994, and Watson 1975**, are all
  paywalled. Watson is the largest loss: his objection is reported, but
  with contradictory attributions.
- **Stump 1988** has a legitimate author-linked copy on PhilArchive, which
  blocks this environment. The owner could fetch it in a browser.
- **The mid-2019 SEP *Compatibilism* revision** holds the wanton/person
  text. It was read only for that section.

## Links

- **[LIT-117](../../record/literature.d/LIT-117.md)** (Enoch, *Agency, Shmagency*, Deferred) is the constitutivist
  target that Velleman's functional proposal invites.
- **[LIT-130](../../record/literature.d/LIT-130.md)** (personal identity and ethics) bears on Velleman 2002.
- **[LIT-202](../../record/literature.d/LIT-202.md)**'s "Frankfurt-style case" is the 1969 device, not the
  hierarchy.

The agent drops out of the causal story in Velleman 1992, and Sen's agency
freedom ([LIT-289](../../record/literature.d/LIT-289.md), second-hand through [LIT-283](../../record/literature.d/LIT-283.md)) is a neighbouring notion. The
record does not yet connect them beyond this sentence.

## The owner's prior-art novelty map, registered in full

*2026-09-29 21:50:47 · curation · record*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-254 — Deferred: already held and listed in the table as held; the directive lapses when its status changes -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: LIT-267 — Proposed: already held and listed in the table as held; the directive lapses when its status changes -->

The owner asked for every reference in their prior-art novelty map to be
registered in this record. The map is a private working document on concepts
as projectors, the linear representation hypothesis and their neighbours.

**How it was done.** Three agents worked in parallel, split by domain:

- quantum foundations, logic and representation theory;
- ML, information theory and the thermodynamics of learning;
- philosophy and linguistics.

For each reference they checked both records, pinned down the exact work and
verified its identifier. Identifiers were verified against Crossref, arXiv or
the publisher. Where no DOI covers the first edition, a stable Internet
Archive URL is used instead: Riesz 1907, Ryle 1949 and Armstrong 1978.

**The result.** The map names 63 works once multi-part works are split:
Aerts–Gabora I and II, Döring–Isham I–IV, Artin–Wedderburn as two papers,
and Cramér–Rao as Rao 1945 and Cramér 1946.

- **6 were already held.** Four were held first-hand: [LIT-262](../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md), [LIT-273](../../record/literature.d/LIT-273.md),
  [LIT-016](../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md) and [LIT-220](../../record/literature.d/LIT-220.md). [LIT-254](../../record/literature.d/LIT-254.md) and [LIT-267](../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md) were also already held.
- **57 are new seeds,** all `Deferred`, from metadata and published
  descriptions. None has been read.

**Held in both records ([ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md)).** Six of the new seeds are also held in the
anthology: Park 2023, Huh 2024, McCandlish 2018, Shwartz-Ziv & Tishby 2017,
Power 2022 and Nanda 2023. The reason for a second entry is the one [ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md)
asks for: this record holds them for the owner's prior-art map, the
anthology for ML practice. Each seed names its anthology entry in its body.

**Near misses the agents caught.** These look held but are not:

- [LIT-263](../../record/literature.d/LIT-263.md) is a *review* of Kochen–Specker, not the 1967 paper.
- [LIT-270](../../record/literature.d/LIT-270.md) is Aerts 2025, not Aerts–Gabora 2005.
- [LIT-175](../../record/literature.d/LIT-175.md) is Worrall 2007, not 1989.
- [LIT-045](../../record/literature.d/LIT-045.md), [LIT-184](../../record/literature.d/LIT-184.md), [LIT-217](../../record/literature.d/LIT-217.md), [LIT-218](../../record/literature.d/LIT-218.md) and [LIT-219](../../record/literature.d/LIT-219.md) are Ladyman or Ross works,
  but not Ladyman 1998 or *Every Thing Must Go*.
- [LIT-042](../../record/literature.d/LIT-042.md) and [LIT-224](../../record/literature.d/LIT-224.md) are not Shannon 1949.

  not Tishby, Pereira & Bialek 1999.

  registered now.

## Close readings of the prior-art novelty map's references

*2026-09-29 23:06:37 · curation · record*

The owner asked for readings of the 57 `Deferred` seeds that registering the
prior-art novelty map added, wherever a work could be found to read.

**How it was done.** Eight agents split the seeds by subject: quantum
cognition and structural realism; thermodynamics of learning; topos quantum
theory (Döring–Isham, Isham–Butterfield); classic mathematics and physics;
interpretability; equivariance and Boolean analysis; learning dynamics and
information theory; and the philosophy and textbook tail. Each worked only from
legitimate copies: arXiv, publishers' free archives, GDZ, Math-Net.Ru, a

the US public domain (renewal records checked). Shadow libraries and
unauthorised uploads were refused even where they were the only copy found.

**The result.** 36 works were read and 21 could not be reached.

**Metadata corrections from the readings.**

**What the readings say about the map.** These findings are for the map's
owner to act on. Nothing in the map was edited.

- **Row 8 (the Stone leg).**
  - Isham–Butterfield I ([LIT-325](../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md)) already owns the chain from Kochen–Specker
    to Stone duality (§2.3).
  - Stone 1936 ([LIT-353](../../record/literature.d/LIT-353.md)) contains no topology, Stone space, duality or
    ultrafilters; those are in Stone 1937, which is not registered.
  - In the finite case, ultrafilters are atoms, which may be faces rather than
    only topes.
- **Orthomodularity and negation.**
  - Birkhoff–von Neumann ([LIT-306](../../record/literature.d/LIT-306.md)) propose the *modular* law, not the
    orthomodular one. Citing them for "orthomodular" is a misattribution.
  - Döring–Isham use a Heyting negation, which clashes with the map's
    orthocomplement rows, and give no finite witness.
  - Kochen–Specker ([LIT-298](../../record/literature.d/LIT-298.md)) prove dimension 3 only. They never state
    "dimension ≥ 3".
- **Row 7 (predicate harmonics and irreps).**
  - "Harmonics = characters" is textbook abelian harmonic analysis
    (O'Donnell, [LIT-346](../../record/literature.d/LIT-346.md)), so KNOWN, not SYNTHESIS. Walsh 1923 ([LIT-300](../../record/literature.d/LIT-300.md)) has
    no characters at all.
  - "Multiplets = degeneracies" is the Schur corollary. Kondor–Trivedi
    ([LIT-305](../../record/literature.d/LIT-305.md)) supply the machinery but never state it, and Peter–Weyl
    ([LIT-329](../../record/literature.d/LIT-329.md)) does not state the converse "degeneracy implies symmetry".
  - Abelian characters give no multiplets. The cube's degeneracies come from
    the nonabelian signed-permutation group, which the equivariance reader
    checked numerically.
  - The equivariance papers ([LIT-314](../../record/literature.d/LIT-314.md), [LIT-305](../../record/literature.d/LIT-305.md), [LIT-319](../../record/literature.d/LIT-319.md)) and Engels et al.
    ([LIT-322](../../record/literature.d/LIT-322.md)) all take the group as given. So "they impose; you detect"
    holds, and Engels' weekday and month circles are the natural validation
    target.
  - Murota et al. ([LIT-352](../../record/literature.d/LIT-352.md)), the nearest algorithmic precedent, has a
    Theorem 3.1(C) that fails over ℝ, the reader checked numerically. It also
    has no noise model.
- **Row 12 (gradient as channel).**
  - McCandlish ([LIT-348](../../record/literature.d/LIT-348.md)) owns batch = gradient SNR and the critical batch. His
    progress law saturates, whereas the map's log(1 + SNR) keeps growing.
  - The channel frame belongs to Xu–Raginsky ([LIT-347](../../record/literature.d/LIT-347.md)), not McCandlish.
  - Shwartz-Ziv–Tishby ([LIT-324](../../record/literature.d/LIT-324.md)) is uncited prior art for "gradient SNR
    organises training".
  - The IB paper ([LIT-338](../../record/literature.d/LIT-338.md)) says nothing about gradients.
- **Row 13.**
  - Goldt–Seifert ([LIT-308](../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) and Still et al. ([LIT-327](../../record/literature.d/LIT-327.md)) bound entropy
    production. They do not support a kT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, since
    heat is due only at erasure.
  - The three "temperatures" (McCandlish's ε/B, Gibbs β, IB β) are formal
    analogies, none of them k_B·T.
- **Rows 2 and 5.**
  - Eckart–Young ([LIT-330](../../record/literature.d/LIT-330.md)) is unique as a matrix only when λ_r > λ_{r+1}, and
    the factors are never unique.
  - Riesz 1907 ([LIT-326](../../record/literature.d/LIT-326.md)) states the representation without proof or
    uniqueness.
  - Park et al.'s ([LIT-304](../../record/literature.d/LIT-304.md)) causal inner product is fixed only by an
    arbitrary choice.
  - None of the three supports a "Riesz-forced unique factorisation".
  - Wick–Wightman–Wigner ([LIT-339](../../record/literature.d/LIT-339.md)) make cross-sector superpositions
    *mixtures*, not truth-value gaps.
- **Structural realism.** Worrall 1989 ([LIT-315](../../record/literature.d/LIT-315.md)) is epistemic structural
  realism, so it is the wrong citation for "to be is to be an invariant of
  structure". Ladyman 1998 ([LIT-342](../../record/literature.d/LIT-342.md)), the ontic source, was unreachable.
- **Aerts–Gabora ([LIT-340](../../record/literature.d/LIT-340.md), [LIT-312](../../record/literature.d/LIT-312.md)).** Their models are single-basis, so the
  map's "non-distributive" gloss should go.
- **Platonic Representation Hypothesis ([LIT-302](../../record/literature.d/LIT-302.md)).** Its measured convergence
  is small (a mutual-kNN score of 0.16), and the proof shows only a shared
  kernel. The map's "PRH-measured" needs these qualifiers.
- **Toy Models ([LIT-323](../../record/literature.d/LIT-323.md)).** The reader's own inference, checked numerically,
  is a bridge to the map: in the efficiently packed shapes the features form
  a tight frame, a rank-one POVM whose weights are the paper's feature
  dimensionalities. That would make superposition a compressed Boolean
  context, a candidate reading of "Boolean shadow".

**Disagreements with the anthology ([ADR-013](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-013.md)).** Several readings found faults in
the anthology's entries for the six dual-held papers. For example:

- The anthology's Park et al. entry reports "four quadruples" where the paper
  has one.
- Its Platonic Representation Hypothesis entry omits the 0.16 ceiling.
- Its grokking entries do not record that the headline run used no weight
  decay, or that dropout also produces grokking.
- Its McCandlish entry claims an "order of magnitude" fit that fails for the
  SVHN models.

Each is in the NOTE concerned, reported and not fixed. They are for an
anthology pass to take up.

**Traps.** The filing script built regex replacements from reading text, and
a backslash in a summary broke it partway through. Use a function as the

<a id="20260929233704"></a>

## Supplemental readings for the prior-art novelty map's misattributions

*2026-09-29 23:37:04 · curation · record*

The close readings of the prior-art novelty map's references
(`record/curation.d/2026/09/29/230637.md`) found several places where the map
cites the wrong work or a work that could not be reached. They were recorded
as findings but not followed up. The owner asked for the follow-up. This batch
registers and reads the works the map should cite instead.

**How it was done.** Three agents shared one brief, split as follows:

- Stone 1937, Husimi, Zaslavsky's announcement and Stanley;
- the two symmetry-detection papers;
- Russo & Zou, Bennett and Earman.

Each gave a verdict on whether its work supplies what the map needs. Only
legitimate sources were used: arXiv, J-STAGE, an author-linked PDF, and the
Internet Archive's public-domain scan of *Trans. AMS* 41.

**Result.** Nine works were registered. Seven were read and two were
unreachable.

**Row 8: Stone duality and topes.**

- **Stone 1937 ([LIT-358](../../record/literature.d/LIT-358.md))** is the source of the topological duality, so
  row 8 should cite it in place of Stone 1936 ([LIT-353](../../record/literature.d/LIT-353.md)). Its Theorems 1, 2 and
  4 give the prime-ideal space as a totally disconnected, locally compact
  Hausdorff space, compact exactly when the ring has a unit. Stone calls this
  a "mathematical equivalence", not a duality, and never states it for
  morphisms. It says nothing about ultrafilters, hyperplanes or regions. The
  paper also contains Stone–Čech, Stone–Weierstrass and Banach–Stone. Stone's
  link to character-group duality (p. 393) is a conjecture in the text, not a
  result. [LIT-353](../../record/literature.d/LIT-353.md) now points at it.
- **Stanley's arrangements notes ([LIT-355](../../record/literature.d/LIT-355.md))** are the readable proof of
  Zaslavsky's theorem that the record lacked. They show that region and face
  counts depend only on the intersection poset. The notes never use "topes"
  and do not cite Zaslavsky, so they are cited *alongside* [LIT-332](../../record/literature.d/LIT-332.md), not
  instead of it.
- **Zaslavsky's announcement ([LIT-359](../../record/literature.d/LIT-359.md))** is open access at the AMS, but
  every route to it was blocked from this session. It stays `Deferred`, and
  anyone with ordinary web access can fetch it.
- **"Ultrafilters ↔ topes"** still has no source. It needs an
  oriented-matroid text plus the owner's own argument, as [NOTE-272](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-272.md) and
  [NOTE-290](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-290.md) said.

**Orthomodularity.** Husimi 1937 ([LIT-357](../../record/literature.d/LIT-357.md)) derives the Birkhoff–von
Neumann lattice from statistical premises. It *uses* the orthomodular law as
an unnamed proof step, but never states or names it. The usual credit to
Husimi is therefore a reading of his axioms. [NOTE-275](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-275.md) now carries that
correction. A source that states the law as an axiom (Kalmbach, or the Piron
line) is still missing. Husimi also raises the "meaningless proposition"
(truth-value gap) reading (p. 769) and declines it. That bears on row 5.

**Row 7: "they impose; you detect".**

- **Lenc & Vedaldi 2015 ([LIT-363](../../record/literature.d/LIT-363.md)).** They fit linear maps on a trained
  network's feature space that realise named image transformations. So
  symmetry *has* been measured in learned representations, and the group acts
  on representation space. That weakens the "where the group acts" distinction
  drawn in [NOTE-274](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-274.md), [NOTE-282](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-282.md) and [NOTE-288](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-288.md).
- **Cohen & Welling 2014 ([LIT-362](../../record/literature.d/LIT-362.md)).** They learn the irreps of a
  commutative group from pairs related by an unknown element, but the group
  class is fixed in advance. This is the "learn irreps from data" prior art.
  The map's "Cohen–Welling" is the 2016 paper, which imposes the group.
- **What survives as novel.** Both papers need paired inputs, and either a
  hypothesised transformation or an assumed group class. Neither looks at an
  operator's spectrum, so degeneracy plays no role in either. The owner's
  claim survives, narrowed to *where the group comes from*: eigenvalue
  multiplicities, with no pairs and no hypothesised group.
- **Two corrections to earlier notes.** [NOTE-282](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-282.md) said abelian symmetries give
  "no degeneracy". That is false over ℝ for SO(2) and ℤ/n with n ≥ 3, whose
  rotation irreps force pairs; that is Cohen & Welling 2014's setting and
  Engels et al.'s ([LIT-322](../../record/literature.d/LIT-322.md)). [NOTE-288](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-288.md)'s relay of Lenc & Vedaldi overstates
  that paper. Both notes now carry dated corrections.

**Row 12: the learner as a channel.** Russo & Zou ([LIT-356](../../record/literature.d/LIT-356.md)) is the
original of the bound that Xu & Raginsky ([LIT-347](../../record/literature.d/LIT-347.md)) extend, so row 12 should
cite both.

- Their Lemma 1 chains information over adaptive steps, and it is the origin
  of [LIT-347](../../record/literature.d/LIT-347.md)'s eq. (36).
- Their Lemma 2 prices one noisy query at ½·log(1 + SNR). That is the nearest
  existing result to the map's C_step = d·log₂(1 + SNR). It covers queries
  answered with added independent noise, not minibatch gradients, so it
  cannot be cited for SGD without a further argument.
- [NOTE-306](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-306.md) stated their quantity in Xu & Raginsky's notation, and now says so.

**Row 13: the heat floor.** Bennett ([LIT-360](../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md)) settles it against the map.

- Only logically irreversible steps carry a cost, and the cost is entropy in
  the environment, which "need not" be heat.
- Bennett calls "an intrinsic cost of order kT for every elementary act of
  information processing" a misconception.
- The defensible form is "k_B T ln 2 of entropy per predicate bit erased or
  overwritten". This agrees with [NOTE-295](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-295.md) and [NOTE-296](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-296.md).
- Bennett gets the title of Landauer 1961 wrong, so cite him for the
  principle's scope and not as a substitute for [LIT-328](../../record/literature.d/LIT-328.md).

**Row 5: superselection and truth-value gaps.**

- **Earman 2008 ([LIT-361](../../record/literature.d/LIT-361.md))** is paywalled and is not on PhilSci-Archive.
  The only copy found was a draft reposted in a third party's reading-group
  folder, which was not used.
- **The truth-value-gap reading** still has no source that asserts it. Husimi
  raises and declines it, and Wick–Wightman–Wigner make cross-sector
  superpositions mixtures ([NOTE-304](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-304.md)).

**Structural realism, which needed no new reading.** The earlier curation
entry said only the unreachable Ladyman 1998 ([LIT-342](../../record/literature.d/LIT-342.md)) could stand in for
Worrall 1989 ([LIT-315](../../record/literature.d/LIT-315.md)) on ontic structural realism. That was wrong: the record
already holds ontic sources, read earlier. They are:

- [LIT-217](../../record/literature.d/LIT-217.md) (Ladyman, "Science, Metaphysics and Structural Realism");
- [LIT-219](../../record/literature.d/LIT-219.md) (Ladyman & Ross, "Patterns All the Way Up");
- [LIT-218](../../record/literature.d/LIT-218.md) (OSR applied to economics);
- [LIT-222](../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md) and [LIT-223](../../record/literature.d/LIT-223.md) (the category-theoretic debate over radical OSR).

The map's "to be is to be an invariant of structure" should be sourced there.

**Traps.** The Wayback copy of Zaslavsky's announcement was refused by this
session's egress policy rather than by the archive. A session with different
network settings may reach it directly.

<a id="20260930015542"></a>

## Signal detection theory, registered and read

*2026-09-30 01:55:42 · curation · record*

The owner asked whether signal detection theory (SDT) is covered in this
record. It was not. The only related entries were Van Trees 1968 ([LIT-351](../../record/literature.d/LIT-351.md), the
owner's prior-art map cites it for row 14's detection model, P(flip) =
Q(γ/σ) with a Cramér–Rao bound), Rao 1945 ([LIT-349](../../record/literature.d/LIT-349.md)) and Cramér 1946 ([LIT-311](../../record/literature.d/LIT-311.md)).
All three are `Deferred` and unreachable. This batch registers the founding
and standard SDT sources and reads the ones that could be reached.

**How it was done.** Two agents shared one brief.

- **One took the statistics and engineering line:** Neyman & Pearson 1933,
  and Peterson & Birdsall.
- **The other took the psychophysics line:** Tanner & Swets 1954, Green &
  Swets 1966, and an open tutorial on the measures.

Each also judged whether its work could stand in for Van Trees on row 14. The
sources used were a public-domain Internet Archive scan of the November 1954
*Psychological Review*, the publisher's own free PDF, and DTIC scans mirrored
in the Internet Archive's US-government documents collection.

**Result.** Five works registered: three read and two unreachable.

- **Peterson & Birdsall 1953 ([LIT-364](../../record/literature.d/LIT-364.md)), Skimmed.**
  - **What was read.** The University of Michigan technical report, Parts I
    and II, registered as the report. The 1954 IRE paper with Fox is its
    journal version, given in the venue. Fox is thanked in the report, and
    becomes an author only in 1954.
  - **Findings.**
    - One receiver that outputs the likelihood ratio is optimal under the
      payoff criterion, the Neyman–Pearson criterion and the posterior
      approach alike.
    - It introduces the ROC and proves that its slope equals the threshold.
    - In white Gaussian noise the log-likelihood ratio is equal-variance
      normal with detection index d = 2E/N₀, and the optimal receiver is a
      matched filter.
    - Its index d is the square of the later d′. It never uses d′ or "ideal
      observer".
- **Tanner & Swets 1954 ([LIT-368](../../record/literature.d/LIT-368.md)), Read.** The founding psychophysics
  citation.
  - It names d′ (as √d, after Peterson & Birdsall), separates sensitivity
    from criterion, and draws the ROC.
  - It gives the optimal criterion β = prior odds × payoff ratio.
  - With three observers it predicts four-alternative accuracy from yes-no
    d′, and rejects the "false alarms are guesses" threshold model. The paper
    says "four" observers once, but only three appear in the data.
- **Stanislaw & Todorov 1999 ([LIT-367](../../record/literature.d/LIT-367.md)), Read.** The compact source for the
  formulas: d′, β, c, A′, B″, A_z, and 2AFC accuracy Φ(d′/√2), each with its
  assumptions. The reader checked the worked example by hand. It gives no d′
  formula for m-alternative choice with m > 2.
- **Neyman & Pearson 1933 ([LIT-365](../../record/literature.d/LIT-365.md)), unreachable.** OpenAlex marks it
  open access, but every Royal Society URL returned a challenge page, and the
  Wayback copy was blocked by this session's egress policy. The only other
  copies were reposts, which were not used. A session with ordinary web access
  should be able to read it.
- **Green & Swets 1966 ([LIT-366](../../record/literature.d/LIT-366.md)), unreachable.** In copyright, and the
  only copy is controlled lending. Its identifier is an Open Library URL,
  since the book has no DOI.

**What the record now says about SDT.** The core of SDT now rests on sources
read first-hand: the likelihood-ratio decision rule, the ROC, the
equal-variance Gaussian model, and the split between sensitivity (d′) and
criterion (β, c).

- The engineering statement is Peterson & Birdsall.
- The psychophysical application is Tanner & Swets.
- The measures are Stanislaw & Todorov.

The likelihood-ratio lemma itself is still second-hand until Neyman &
Pearson is read. The only thematic link to earlier holdings is [LIT-099](../../record/literature.d/LIT-099.md) on
framing effects in perception.

**Row 14 of the map.**

- **The detection half can now cite Peterson & Birdsall instead of Van
  Trees.** The equal-prior error Q(√d/2) = Q(d′/2) follows in one line from
  its eqs. 4.3–4.8, but it is never printed. So it is cited as derived, not
  quoted. [LIT-351](../../record/literature.d/LIT-351.md) now says so.
- **Tanner & Swets and Stanislaw & Todorov supply the tail-at-criterion
  form.** Error rates are Gaussian tails at a criterion measured in noise SDs,
  which is the Q(γ/σ) form, and Stanislaw & Todorov print the 2AFC result.
- **The Cramér–Rao half still has no reachable source.** None of the three
  has estimation theory.

**Traps.** Royal Society and DTIC pages sit behind challenges from here, even
for open-access items. The Internet Archive's government-documents mirror of
DTIC scans is the legitimate route for pre-1960 US government technical
reports.
